clean_body: Too often, home care workers are overlooked and underappreciated by lawmakers who treat them like a budget number instead of the lifeline they are. Peter, I recently visited a home care provider in Anaheim to talk about the struggles she and so many others are facing in California. The bottom line is simple: home care workers do not get paid enough. She told me about caring for her daughter, who is blind and disabled, and her sister, who is a veteran living with trauma related injuries. These are people she loves deeply, and who rely on her every single day. But the programs that make this care possible, like Medi-Cal, are under attack. Her daughter and sister are losing the services they depend on. Home care providers can’t afford to stand by and do nothing. Too often, they are overlooked and underappreciated by lawmakers who treat them like a budget number, instead of the lifeline they are. And there’s a pattern here: this work is done by moms, grandmas, women. Over and over again, politicians assume they will keep doing it for nothing. There is always money for something else, but never enough for health care, nursing care, or mental health care. I’m running for governor because California can do better. We can expand health care access instead of cutting it. We can make sure our home care workers get paid what they deserve for the critical work they do. I’m running to be a champion for all Californians—especially those who politicians overlook all too often. Thank you, Katie Porter P.S. Katie is running to be California’s next governor because California and our country need a leader who will stand up to Trump to lower costs, protect our rights, and combat climate change.

President Barack Obama shakes hands with Illinois House Speaker Michael Madigan as he arrives to address the Illinois General Assembly at the state Capitol in Springfield on Feb.10, 2016. (Mandel Ngan / Getty/AFP)
By Illinois Review

Former Illinois House Speaker Michael J. Madigan — the most powerful Democrat machine boss in modern state history — is now reportedly trying to convince President Donald J. Trump to pardon his federal prison sentence.

The request would be astonishing from any politician. Coming from Madigan, it is almost unbelievable.

For decades, Madigan championed everything Trump fought against: relentless tax hikes, sanctuary-state policies, protection for illegal immigrants, and a political machine that crushed working families while enriching insiders.

Madigan didn’t just operate inside the system — he built the machine that drove Illinois into fiscal ruin.

No one in modern Illinois history raised taxes more aggressively. Under his control, residents were hit repeatedly. Since 2011, Madigan personally pushed or approved more than 70 bills that raised taxes or fees — income taxes, gas taxes, vehicle fees, cigarette taxes, business taxes, sports-betting taxes, and more.

The 2011 income-tax hike alone drained billions from family budgets. In 2017, Madigan forced through another massive increase by overriding Gov. Bruce Rauner’s veto. And in 2019, he backed doubling the gas tax — now automatically rising every year.

And when a Democratic governor refused to go along with Madigan’s tax-hike agenda, Madigan moved to destroy him.

Rod Blagojevich openly rejected Madigan’s plan to raise taxes on working families. Madigan responded exactly as a machine boss would: he led the effort to impeach him.

Months before the FBI’s predawn raid, Madigan circulated a detailed 14-page memo outlining the political case to remove Blagojevich — essentially pre-writing the roadmap for his downfall.

Madigan made noise — and Robert Mueller listened.

(Julia Demaree Nikhinson/AP)
By Illinois Review

Illinois Republicans are now sounding the alarm about sanctuary cities, migrant crime, and the collapse of border security.

But there’s one inconvenient truth they prefer to ignore: in 2017, the Illinois Republican Party praised the very bill that turned Illinois into a sanctuary state — all while President Donald J. Trump was just months into his first term and making illegal immigration and border security the centerpiece of his administration.

The bill was the Illinois TRUST Act (SB 31), a Democrat-written sanctuary measure that restricts state and local law enforcement from cooperating with federal immigration authorities. It limits when police can communicate with ICE, bans arrests based solely on immigration status, and blocks ICE detainers that lack a judicial warrant.

It became the legal blueprint for Illinois’ sanctuary status.

This season usually fills our home with joy, family, prayers, and warmth.
But this year feels different.
_This year, our daughter Nancy is walking through fire._
**[And we have one Christmas wish, just one,_that we hope you’ll help us fulfill._](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/wkVSNjrJ-U0mJ9pwWOVWFq3RMW-PFPl_NwLhiqPamOLyROLmS_5vIZnhFbYsBVLelAqe0RJO1-yoS8UPjUwpLpD4eduMGjk64QOYhoC1epqnESxpFzOxgtq0BN5xKpbTagZ2AgkM5WQxZxT1Ihwj4Fzoszas0q4g9mYW4-sB79CiEhiWuDNwAcDY25cqCPvDmQiV4vu8HS01WvFOhDida9yUKqYbrYXRrdA5dPdxLJDLBYWXu8rvKy1xWF3A-ObCx2LQPMXBcyBUIfa_pSclCrReKdNmGB6anAKgGjOVsBklwx-OIirJV4AttLndrxkAM1BX5NO1Rn_ODNNzHQ5uThqcUueD2kpQ51z2hLc3TZD4F2jl65-AbzuV16pnfnACUZDO0b5-3AeGc-nM5ACboAhgbG8hMmIb-4NjsNVZIfU2McY7kDszC59O_F5v_tUu-mcp12CU96Dl_voWt2T_rdClQ2-KS6BRDAxL6XF9Iuojni8FOUd_vm-OydS9qXjed5RnI0XssllGrEArLUzAKy89H-r_Mr953mdmLoeKxMBapGpXeKqKxTqBKoPhzRSpCdQh4Q0fqcvfzIrQn7aHI3hYEx04lgOQYrCDuWu8ibTP8Twnzd2cGSxzfZIQYeYVaPGdcKS8JZfv1QX9DIXckqSy3um1KwVPNS5zSFaHkvB987FdVALXSIXf4Ssek4WE-W45c4do-iGstmiX9gb21atXdl4P4FJl4X03riozH5G2rhZ1DV7n6kD1Qc585MoCn1smvOs0yGhFKSneOhzYVz_w5y6xIEqn8M_yWgfY3Oxcv49KtMAxrZlVB0HC4LAqAHe22FQozQNHPJWbn9SwA0tlaHM5MhA/_UG2TekVvCvTDLozG3RTCR3CLa4U5hA0/15)__**
But first, let us tell you something about her.
[**When our daughter Nancy was 17, she dropped out of high school.**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/DtlSWAqgQpHyiZ9fk5l_YQ_Lu6Ue5H0ldNET-hivk18wMJAg8vK-4D2yqdEfmFDDP7bA3870AwvMY-A9FwQBwOSM-WVdehEFuVifuLGNhdMEBqJwXAmCVz0UiqZH1PShmQxCp46icCCARdz0tqWh9QWJWKf4ywbt1Jye0cXBHVumoaA-YjKqbKh5WBMBFnqLYDEw7SV7Pn7iXHBi1tPTkWvBenGBPYNdBE9GiNRrQ3Crif6vypYd6_fJGGpeyJnc-RMyvyLv5YF7_EzLUOQh8jyOG24kCdvmquLrb4EHelksmwp0JShU-gAouQudzzYzM49zw_aexCaCwjTuRQpXVrgysIPg3zpWFEdHgjHxWp19qYCvpjtSmQ6b-TLVkD4I5Lbp7vSi45IZAU9c3PK2HNHhHPZW3y7oRxqwVGlcoCqjNoL_4AXTSdHBt1_dpoa7imm3g6CgH1RTTac-t8o5nklQI68UYmYw1AULlHDQURBmHBeS7oNcMbZV8e5lASToF1dnokF-KwZrYACR67LY7DqQg3JXyQpnWMa5CoDY8KlekfnILRO12fAx9Bfu3HFAI_0OxLZi-_uV8NtoOee-SrndJqv-M_QPLZae9aY2HnomKmUTwf-hHGii5bmC6XEZMZMrOPgi9GlDlzXvdFiHj8Lcl7NkKLmW_jwXxvEYrO_Wased5V8Nt4RVgTzhrYqH6rarO4t-iO3VXsTgXJeUva3f2bk6hEFMj7CK-Zj3w03jUvWLgqikSQHcrl78oMdGEdWr0A4gfVG98sxn_QeuVBbHtUyyigGjSbcTb1rUPIru6fep4oEDcVyohxJ6OV-XRxyfKVYLzXJYErrQ6W69oAY4BStGUoM/1CHddefllh59BMStY2cRT4kX9RN0q-0N/15)
We remember the night she told us. _Her hands were shaking. She thought she’d disappointed everyone she loved._
But we raised her to believe that setbacks don’t define you—**how you rise does.**
[**With a WWII veteran for a father and a schoolteacher for a mother, she grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again:**](https://links.iterable.com/s/c/DW4JjFDgMtP9widI50IrdShxo9a2M-LDH6qoYbqO4AgYjHmCReR15xhlkhalCQoE1-6Wg1at6CZAinDowQhV9gfecYSC_MCqmPhRRs1uUCvGAYmTRireYVEY5Xp-556nD8UpztVMsAfA4ImQXwvLI3MMeuom1ZeHg5lZFqT9YMSAW0b7mpEyp0WyxWgpefE5mf6obc9HrIx2Y0gr0tJP5fsCBQFGKHCLf9vuPB5Uj3rrAKNEd6_s8EpcrMHmPo8qlTdLG0LaNRFy4z7R-23GatUrvJPUrAz9rDM62weoj4z2xQKG2MyYr3T6Gl6sThN94kM7Cjd3YBu1QYMxPmFP7o4uKLADA5fgCG-KOgisaj2kUjQHR_wGfEWLKkdz9WZ3V8_4pkniPFYjHvxO5R2pEWLrECpS7G23YZHfENwRtDCXvPyrsZOXcU4wpPVRonHRmx9d1nHcAPG-GkNDYSYM3O36hQsj5XDiOv2aSM8gXj5u1i59OKC-Cn5O9eSUaytn-yxnO6UwHM_ZExVeriM1RswhRnyF5oAuXJpJNbRnBYWCpQwWbP0DV_m-6-hdrQ6tmgUEzYZwe9ReNIvynoZ10_00dCk6GJB00xDm4b5mzuiUcyyPD3lY-PkFV4o4oEeFhQiFHdiPSlHR_h3xKn8uzUFXam-DocZ5JE9HAnyWxd9PQA-SQsSNBTe73ElSFrf9CztgwyP7Ab1M5HvffYf5ZWq8xsrvbnxQzaWTqBs_OPQKUc6agbxPIkvlk18ocNnRJRpmjKDgq1WlRSiVRCQ1Fcya4r-2ib6MvPy5gE578wHPwQ1mjiWC575HGL2q9jekXa5bXa7qaPYj189JSyCSvEe3UGgKgMA/lzZeclF9UZlnGy2BYYC2rqBAJ5o5WruF/15)
👉 _Never quit._
👉 _Never run from the truth._
👉 _And never let anyone tell you that _**you are less than what God made you to be.**__
So we gave her a choice:
**Go back to school... or get a job.**
Most kids in that situation fall apart. But not Nancy. She picked herself up, took a job at Waffle House, and fought her way back.

**High school dropout. Waffle House waitress. First woman to graduate from The Citadel. Single mom. Fighter.** **Nancy Mace wasn’t born into power. She built her own business. She raised two kids on her own. And when the Left came for everything she believed in, she stood her ground.Now, she’s running for Governor of South Carolina. Nancy Mace is a battle-tested conservative who’s walked through fire and come out swinging. In Congress, she’s been one of President Trump’s fiercest allies, fighting to secure our border, protect our daughters, and stop the Left’s sick agenda dead in its tracks. **She’s not here to make friends. She’s here to make history.** Nancy is fighting to:

* Prosecute violent criminals and pedophiles with zero leniency
* Crack down on sanctuary sheriffs who let illegal aliens roam free
* Defund radical public universities that indoctrinate, not educate
* Reform education so students learn how to think—not what to think
* Work hand-in-hand with President Trump to put South Carolina FIRST

Through every hardship, Nancy never gave up. And now she’s ready to do what she’s always done: roll up her sleeves, take the heat, and lead from the front. **South Carolina is worth fighting for. And Nancy Mace is just getting started.**

| | ******Friend,** The **Washington Times** just broke a story that should alarm every voter in Colorado: **Lauren Boebert used campaign funds to go to a Kid Rock concert.** And while the behavior is disappointing, it is sadly **not surprising**.
Because this is exactly the kind of choice she makes when she thinks no one is paying attention. And let me be clear about something:
**Using campaign funds for personal entertainment is illegal.**
Not questionable.
Not unethical.
Illegal. When a leader shows you their priorities, believe them. The heckling during the State of the Union.
The theatrics and shouting matches.
The public meltdowns and family scandals.
The mean-spirited division that helps no one. We all remember the theater........ Every time she steps into the spotlight, she proves the same truth: **She is not here to serve - she is here to perform.** And while she performs, real life gets harder for the people she ignores. Parents are choosing between groceries and childcare.
Farmers are fighting consolidation, drought, and rising costs.
Working families are stretched to the breaking point. Yet instead of doing the job she was elected to do, instead of honoring the trust people placed in her, she uses donor money on a concert. Not outreach.
Not advocacy.
Not constituent support. A concert. Another headline.
Another distraction.
Another embarrassment for Colorado's 4th District. But here is the deeper truth.
This scandal is not just about one night at a concert.
**It exposes a complete lack of integrity, accountability, and respect for the people she represents.** Colorado deserves better than this spectacle.
Colorado deserves a representative who understands responsibility. And that is why I am running. Not because I ever wanted to be a politician.
But because I come from a world where **legal and ethical boundaries matter** , where **hard work matters** , and where trust is something you do not ever get to throw away. I did not come from political circles.
I came from **shops, farms, machine rooms, night shifts, and long weeks** spent grinding to give my kids a fair shot. **Working-class values are not my slogan - they built me.**
They shaped my character.
They shaped my discipline.
They shaped my respect for the people who put their trust in me. And that is the difference. A working-class, grassroots movement can defeat her - because we are everything she is not. If we want to replace spectacle with service,
If we want to end this embarrassing circus,

clean_body: This district deserves a leader shaped by real work, not endless spectacle. | | | ****Friend, The Washington Times just broke a story that should alarm every voter in Colorado: Lauren Boebert used campaign funds to go to a Kid Rock concert. And while the behavior is disappointing, it is sadly not surprising. Because this is exactly the kind of choice she makes when she thinks no one is paying attention. And let me be clear about something: Using campaign funds for personal entertainment is illegal. Not questionable. Not unethical. Illegal. When a leader shows you their priorities, believe them. The heckling during the State of the Union. The theatrics and shouting matches. The public meltdowns and family scandals. The mean-spirited division that helps no one. We all remember the theater........ Every time she steps into the spotlight, she proves the same truth: She is not here to serve - she is here to perform. And while she performs, real life gets harder for the people she ignores. Parents are choosing between groceries and childcare. Farmers are fighting consolidation, drought, and rising costs. Working families are stretched to the breaking point. Yet instead of doing the job she was elected to do, instead of honoring the trust people placed in her, she uses donor money on a concert. Not outreach. Not advocacy. Not constituent support. A concert. Another headline. Another distraction. Another embarrassment for Colorado's 4th District. But here is the deeper truth. This scandal is not just about one night at a concert. It exposes a complete lack of integrity, accountability, and respect for the people she represents. Colorado deserves better than this spectacle. Colorado deserves a representative who understands responsibility. And that is why I am running. Not because I ever wanted to be a politician. But because I come from a world where legal and ethical boundaries matter , where hard work matters , and where trust is something you do not ever get to throw away. I did not come from political circles. I came from shops, farms, machine rooms, night shifts, and long weeks spent grinding to give my kids a fair shot. Working-class values are not my slogan - they built me. They shaped my character. They shaped my discipline. They shaped my respect for the people who put their trust in me. And that is the difference. A working-class, grassroots movement can defeat her - because we are everything she is not. If we want to replace spectacle with service, If we want to end this embarrassing circus, If we want leadership grounded in honesty, not attention-seeking, Then we must build a campaign powered by people, not politics. I am asking you directly ~ Every contribution is a choice: A choice for integrity over illegality. A choice for service over spectacle. A choice for a Colorado that can finally hold its head high again. And before I close, I want to leave you with the truth behind this entire campaign: I'm John Padora - a working dad. I come from the world she has forgotten. I'm built different - and that is exactly why we can win this together. ~ If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | ---|--- | ---|--- | ~~ ---|--- Let us show that a grassroots movement built on honesty, lived experience and working-class values can rise above fear, division and the politics of the powerful. However, Americans are pushing back. Last month, California fired the opening blow of the Democratic counter-salvo with their vote to pass Proposition 50, a ballot measure that gives CA a fair congressional map to counter Trump's gerrymandering push.
But California alone won't be enough. To save our Democracy, blue states like Colorado must pick up the torch, join the fight, and meet this moment head on.
This is why Fair Fight Colorado is proud to announce that we are introducing the ballot measure that will give every Coloradan a chance to vote on a new Congressional map.
We have the power to level the playing field and counter Trump's power grab with fair maps that will put power back in the hands of the people but it will require an astronomically expensive push to get this on the ballot and in front of Colorado voters.
MAGA is about to throw everything they've got into stopping us and we need to brace for impact. The only way MAGA can survive 2026 is if they rig the game.

The GOP is moving fast. Gerrymandered maps have passed in Texas, North Carolina, Missouri, and a push for redistricting is underway in Indiana and Florida with more red states soon to follow.
This is an existential crisis. No matter how unpopular Trump becomes, if left unchecked, MAGA will create enough new red seats to ensure their House majority is insurmountable making it impossible for Dems to reclaim the House.
However, Americans are pushing back. Last month, California fired the opening blow of the Democratic counter-salvo with their vote to pass Proposition 50, a ballot measure that gives CA a fair congressional map to counter Trump's gerrymandering push.
But California alone won't be enough. To save our Democracy, blue states like Colorado must pick up the torch, join the fight, and meet this moment head on.
This is why Fair Fight Colorado is proud to announce that we are introducing the ballot measure that will give every Coloradan a chance to vote on a new Congressional map.
We have the power to level the playing field and counter Trump's power grab with fair maps that will put power back in the hands of the people but it will require an astronomically expensive push to get this on the ballot and in front of Colorado voters.
MAGA is about to throw everything they've got into stopping us and we need to brace for impact. ## US Seizes Venezuelan Oil Tanker
The U.S. [seized an oil tanker off Venezuela's coast](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9utDAQxJ_GdEbe5d9H4eJr6C5tSmSz68OJwSdsDnFPH3F5hHQjjWY0v_m8jTfjg1_vH2ZhnV0cVz5S4Jx5G_eU2L84ZbN-83aYc4nW2JN4RIWNBJQAIxkfzrEuSDtm5KpgDV3b1A1ArYpZM022ImzanlsD6KivCNiojipSvXWF11cbIACAaqp_pYW-VZMl1WHXM5GoFZPPcSu_ol_zzC6c8clbOcWlCHrO-ZFE9V_gIHA4jqOcbLooLl_gcEmBwy6TfOOQjD7IXyYZnZN5ZjlFk7KMTj555dfOwci87ctDJnNe6WLT9Dh8CD61najVfTE-vAfkP7321PgTAAD__7Z7g-0) on Wednesday, described by President Trump as the "largest one ever seized," targeting Nicolás Maduro's government. The [Coast Guard-led operation](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUk2PmzAU_DXmBsIGAjlwiLZKT7uXdNUjMvZz8rrGD9kmKXvob6_4qNRIvfU0o7Fn3jzw99fuVaJFd32TA7TRUOfgESzECL6bQgD8hBCl-wD_kPNAvexnDZ3IRZVykXLeaYl27spEtwZAQJFAy-tDVVacl3lya2VZF7op4KibuhF9w6sK6t4cD01Zqh6qBNsljQvOOc-rosl6fjzkqtd5LeojaM3KHDRG8tkPQhdvYOxMd_CZoiGx7S3GMbDixMSZibPs1bJBdqXlmInz-4WJ8wM9XCL5mYlz9NMwplNI1-V0SmjTbcOUjEkVyRDTOzj4nMDKlItGHHlZciYKVpx-seIU4WdkxZdvN2CiEvmSM_mNP2RYUUnvEfTK7Y79vELcbe_ZZcWXZeDKvk7SP1vAGPLboXSbFKZxJB__nfkm76vwslmUIq_RXbc7tIl_hmcrIWNQobRP7R3tM6d4I798pb8TFA0DuO3GOPUWlZ2fK470sfUh91RPkdMYcVfJ7C5y84BxzhLf6vGB1mI41KzMr4NEu_7l-F9P896K3wEAAP__gL7qRA) was executed in international waters without incident, according to Attorney General Pam Bondi, who said the vessel had been transporting sanctioned oil from Venezuela and Iran for years. Trump said the U.S. will "keep" the oil and suggested more seizures may follow as part of his pressure campaign to remove Maduro from power. ## Ike Dike Contracts Awarded
Engineering firms in Dallas and Nebraska have been [awarded contracts](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGutCAUBOCnwU4DRxAtKP7Gbv_2lgblqGRRCJxdd9_-ZvcVbjPNJN8k83ObbtYHf27_7YGGXmucTrxKQCLMU7KU_XIvZF8pxxSLDbZQjmUCDqoWUAsxOevDe5KVMzN3g6jQCN0pqaTUqtrNIOYVdDeoee2XRaKTYp7bQfeDQuyBV958MAFCCOCC66bVQzs7ZVvuuMO-Y5Kj8xRzQzsSvmxZwzs-MTdLPKpgdqJUWPuPwchgvK6rWfYcz0_LYNweYa2XaAsxGG0mvwRkMPo71u4TX7BeH6fz51ZTfhypBgGtEEo3aU9VNi5dPgRfOs0k3w7rw3eZ_vbX08BvAAAA___fQ4Aq) to design components of the Coastal Texas Project, or "Ike Dike"—a proposed coastal barrier that would protect the entrance to the Houston Ship Channel from storm surges. A Texas A&M professor [suggested the ambitious project](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykUL2S2yAQfhrU4YGVZM4FRRq6S5tSs2ZXEjEWGliffG-f0b1Cmq_6_v98Tp-YctqW3_hkL--5TBsfLbMI12lHqSk-muB7r2UvDTM2qaVNYGDUFrS1E2HK39PQkb8butmOvXXXcRiHwY3d6pFdnGFE-oiGr72BGW_z0Ns7mXF04LrkTzML1low1rhL7279nUbsDRnij6saDFOSUi-ysvAb25y_yxfXSyzPLvtVZG-q_6UgKAjHcVxiTvEBa3k1KdvJUhDOWQrCj15BODMVBAsKghkUhFg2qRilaTywEpOWoolbWja9oHDTuJGm18ZNz6Xq5ZVnHQs20enBmk7Ya_nLURSErnraj5RzalenBrM8MeWfvvJ_L395-BcAAP__VdSS0Q) in the aftermath of Hurricane Ike in 2008, and state lawmakers established the Gulf Coast Protection District in 2021. So far, nearly $1 billion in state funding and $5.5 million in federal funding have been allocated for the project. Dallas-based Jacobs Solutions will design a [series of floodgates](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLEOpCAURb8GOww8UaSg2MZutt3SPOU5soNiAMeZv9-4yX7BNre4Jzm5ub8e4wN98PvzJ25ky2eJ405XDlQKpfHAkvz8ygU_R4pHzBgwlxTzCAJaLoFLOTr04TuqytlJOCMrslJ3rWqV0m212okA-qWbXT8vpB0YoRugzhkyAhdDlbe3TIKUEoQUum60aSbXYiOccNR3TAlyvsRUl5UKfTAv4RvflOo5blWwaylHZs0PBgOD4bqu-rXG84YMBkzFz4EYDFvc6ctgmM7sd8qZwbDGM5e4838V_x3PtGNgMPgXcXfHkeIz3ew8HJZbBH3L-0ZO2hByoUTHldKC9zMAV4aAsGsnBX2VrDsuH4LPnWZKPDf04e_m8n9Pvy38CQAA___o7JJq) spanning the two-mile waterway between Galveston Island and Bolivar Peninsula, while Omaha-based HDR has been contracted to build up the dune system along both shorelines. The cost estimate for the Ike Dike is currently $57-60 billion, and it could take up to 20 years to complete. The plan proposed by the Corps of Engineers calls for the federal government to fund 65% of the project.

The [announcement](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDtu6zAQRVdDdRaGP1MqWDzgQZ3TphRGnrFNhDIVcuDP7gM7S0h_cA_u-TzMB0w5Xc8fuHKUx6nMV763zCJc5w2lpuNXE3xstWylYcYmtbTZgPE7bXZaz4QpP2fXUVyARt1x1GHvnXcu-O4SBzsyLeTBB2TyHI4Mhuw4eL9YB6FL8TWmjdbagIbQ2zDahTxaICAe9soBU5JSe7mw8APbKT_LjWt_LGuX40Vka8r-U2ZSZpLtTv2b6s_lpsz0-rMyJVRmqpwZG7cXaqfK38r-_7XDgF2NtN1Tzqntg3JwXjHlt0P-VuYWzU8AAAD__7f9dzM) cited the 1956 Federal Airborne Hunting Act, which bans the use of aircraft to "take or attempt to take wildlife, or aid in the act of fishing." | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

body:
Peter, this NJ Spotlight News headline isn’t good. It’s also not that “shocking” to any of us who live here and encounter this problem on a near-daily basis.
| | [ ]()
---
Peter, This NJ Spotlight News [headline](https://xtz223.keap-link006.com/v2/click/6a5c3c63b910eb3c625eb01a5a9b9c1c/eJyNkEFPwzAMhf-Lz83SZlRAb9M0TVW3HRCcUVitNaN1osRdKVP_OxmgnUDa1f7ee34-AyNp4rKGAj74U6k5JOBxb5xB4qUl1vvvrcrvsnmWQGvofe1t76A4_ym-ApfxQ54-JsCjw4g8Py2WVblbv27KXRVJp33MuM1HZfnVZ7VdlBuYpn-NsTO8OkXvAAX7Hi-NahNb8YtvI98wu1BIOQzDjI7BWW7NoWHCIcysP0iVqlym95KOorEdthiCoL57Qx9EvFn0TmgWWSpG1F40UStjqnYOqf59WYXjT_b0BVOMdMc=) isn’t good. It’s also not that “shocking” to any of us who live here and encounter this problem on a near-daily basis.
---
|
---
The article reports this represents an 8% increase from last year, and an overall 10-year high. The number of homeless who are “unsheltered” is up 15%. The report spent a lot of time blaming federal policies and a few cuts to state programs, but no time discussing what has actually made housing and living SO unaffordable in the state of New Jersey. Irresponsible spending, bloated bureaucracy, and ineffective and corrupt “leadership” in Trenton. Or, in a word, years of one-party rule by a party that doesn’t know how to govern, balance a budget, or operate efficiently and has instead treated taxpayers like a blank check. Some New Jerseyans have the means to rent a U-Haul and get out of town. Many who don’t have that luxury are finding themselves homeless – including a disproportionate percentage of the state’s Black population who the Democratic party has always purported to advocate for. Trenton created this problem. It’s laughable to expect them to solve it. As we discussed last week, local solutions may be the key – and not just government ones. But local governments and locally based organizations, non-profits, churches and communities are much better situated to understand and address their own homeless population than broad, sweeping statewide policies. That said, smarter, fiscally conservative policies statewide would lift the crushing weight of high costs and high taxes from most New Jerseyans. But Trenton under Leftist leadership has always been averse to taking responsibility and that looks unlikely to change. So what can we do locally? Or personally? Consider putting an extra few pairs of mittens and scarves in your trunk to hand out to a homeless person or panhandler we encounter on a chilly day, or buying a hot cup of coffee for someone trying to stay warm. Because government intervention can never replace human kindness and decency. For New Jersey, Elizabeth Nader

name: Jon Ossoff
subject: What do they expect people to do?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Jon Ossoff for Senate
body:
#

**They have no plan. They _STILL_ have no plan.**
Peter, my team and I hear every single day from Georgians who are absolutely terrified.
They’re facing 100%, 200%, 300% increases in their health care premiums if Republicans in Congress allow Affordable Care Act credits to expire.
My constituents can’t afford this. Some can’t _survive_ it.
Imagine losing health insurance in the middle of chemotherapy because rich and powerful politicians refuse to help you.
_If you’re sick, what do Republicans expect you to do?_
They don’t have an answer.
*****
These Republican Senators walk through the gilded halls of Congress and treat this like a game, completely oblivious to the fact that this is life or death for our constituents.
At Trump’s bidding, they spent trillions of dollars on tax cuts for the rich while they were slashing Medicaid, but they're all tied up in knots on a fundamental moral question: whether Americans should be able to afford health care.
_It’s unacceptable._ **But the truth is that as long as Republicans control Congress, they are going to continue to come after our health care to cut taxes for the rich.**
*****
We know MAGA’s election playbook: Lie. Enrage. Distract.
But we’ve beaten them before — _right here in Georgia._
We defeated an entrenched GOP incumbent by staying on offense and organizing a turnout effort totally unprecedented in its scale and intensity.
Now, in these midterms we face our next test. And it won’t be easy.
I’m the only Democratic U.S. Senator up for reelection in a state Trump won.
MAGA wants me defeated and gone.
Help me defeat them in a landslide. Help fight back.
**[Please contribute to my campaign today.**](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251211-1-f&t=1&akid=1248%2E5691347%2E3U7r1Y)
With gratitude,
Jon Ossoff

👋 Wait! Before you go... 👋
At the end of this month, Jon Ossoff is facing the most important public fundraising deadline of his campaign so far. After it passes, we will be legally required to report how much we’ve raised and how many people donated.
**It is very important that we put up a big number to show Trump, our opponents, and the media that our campaign is fired up and ready to start 2026 strong.**
**[Please use this link to give $5 or whatever you can to Jon’s reelection campaign before our biggest FEC fundraising deadline of the entire campaign so far. Thank you.](https://act.electjon.com/go/32?c0=ossoff-em-dec25.lXrKfY&refcode=em251211-1-f&t=2&akid=1248%2E5691347%2E3U7r1Y)**

Talking at a press conference are, from left, state Senate Minority Leader John Curran, R-Woodridge, Sen. Darby Hills, R-Barrington Hills, and Sen. Erica Harriss, R-Glen Carbon. (Photo courtesy of the Illinois Senate)
By Illinois Review

Illinois Republicans have warned for years that their greatest weakness isn’t always Democrats – it’s the lack of courage within their own caucus. And few episodes illustrate that better than what happened on October 30, 2025, when freshman State Sen. Darby Hills, R-Barrington Hills, walked off the Senate floor and hid during the most consequential immigration vote of the year.

Multiple lawmakers, staffers, and lobbyists share the same story: as debate closed on House Bill 1312 – the Safety and Liberation Together (SALT) Act – Hills abruptly left the Senate chamber. Witnesses say she ducked into the bathroom. Others say she fled down the hallway. But the outcome is undeniable: when the vote was called, she was gone.

While every single Republican senator voted NO, Darby Hills alone was recorded as “NV” – No Vote. She was the only GOP legislator who failed to stand against the largest sanctuary expansion in Illinois history.

|
Peter,
The streets of Chicago feel right different now.
Unmarked vans prowl at night--masked ICE agents snatching neighbors in silence. Protesters are dragged across pavement by masked federal agents whose names are hidden behind black tape. Soldiers march through city intersections meant for kids on bikes and buses to work.
At food banks across America, recently laid off workers wait in line. Families scrape together meals as grocery prices skyrocket.
Children fall asleep hungry. Seniors cut their pills in half, praying it's enough to last the week.
This is Trump's America--and it's only been 12 months.
But in November, there was a beacon of hope.
Across the country, Democrats won landslide victories. Not the kind propped up by corporate donors or political dynasties--but led by a new generation of Democrats, unfazed by Trump's fascist threats, determined to defend democracy and deliver for the people suffering most.

|
They came from every faith, every color, every corner of America--a generation forged in crisis but united in purpose. And together, they dominated Republicans from coast to coast, determined to rebuild this nation for the working class.
I saw that energy firsthand when I worked for Zohran Mamdani during the primary in New York City. The establishment spent millions trying to destroy our movement--but our campaign was powered by people, and we won anyway.
That same exact spirit brought me home to Chicago to work for Bushra Amiwala.
And I'm seeing it again. The same fire. The same defiance. The same hope.
Bushra's campaign isn't fueled by big donors--it's powered by neighbors, students, and working people who believe in a better future for America. While establishment campaigns write checks, Bushra is building a movement.
When ICE began terrorizing our neighbors, Bushra stood by their side even in the face of tear gas and rubber bullets. When AIPAC poured hundreds of thousands into our opponent's campaign, Bushra outraised them with grassroots donations from ordinary people. And when others paid canvassers to collect signatures, our entirely volunteer-led team hit the streets--door by door, block by block--until we got Bushra on the ballot.
This is what democracy looks like in the hands of a new generation.
Now we need to keep building. The stakes are too high to let up for even a day. clean_body: The streets of Chicago feel right different now. | | | | | == | Peter, The streets of Chicago feel right different now. Unmarked vans prowl at night--masked ICE agents snatching neighbors in silence. Protesters are dragged across pavement by masked federal agents whose names are hidden behind black tape. Soldiers march through city intersections meant for kids on bikes and buses to work. At food banks across America, recently laid off workers wait in line. Families scrape together meals as grocery prices skyrocket. Children fall asleep hungry. Seniors cut their pills in half, praying it's enough to last the week. This is Trump's America--and it's only been 12 months. But in November, there was a beacon of hope. Across the country, Democrats won landslide victories. Not the kind propped up by corporate donors or political dynasties--but led by a new generation of Democrats, unfazed by Trump's fascist threats, determined to defend democracy and deliver for the people suffering most. | | == | They came from every faith, every color, every corner of America--a generation forged in crisis but united in purpose. And together, they dominated Republicans from coast to coast, determined to rebuild this nation for the working class. I saw that energy firsthand when I worked for Zohran Mamdani during the primary in New York City. The establishment spent millions trying to destroy our movement--but our campaign was powered by people, and we won anyway. That same exact spirit brought me home to Chicago to work for Bushra Amiwala. And I'm seeing it again. The same fire. The same defiance. The same hope. Bushra's campaign isn't fueled by big donors--it's powered by neighbors, students, and working people who believe in a better future for America. While establishment campaigns write checks, Bushra is building a movement. When ICE began terrorizing our neighbors, Bushra stood by their side even in the face of tear gas and rubber bullets. When AIPAC poured hundreds of thousands into our opponent's campaign, Bushra outraised them with grassroots donations from ordinary people. And when others paid canvassers to collect signatures, our entirely volunteer-led team hit the streets--door by door, block by block--until we got Bushra on the ballot. This is what democracy looks like in the hands of a new generation. Now we need to keep building. The stakes are too high to let up for even a day. subject: The First Real Threat to Citizens United Is Coming from Montana
body:
While Congress stalls and courts enable overreach, one state may have uncovered the path to restore democratic control.
| | | | |
---
| What Is In This Newsletter?

* Montana Steps Up Against Citizens United
* Progressive Strategies NW Data: Hispanic Voter Turnout
* Twelve Billion Dollar Bailout, What a Buffoon

---
| |
---
| Have we finally found a way to deal a death blow to Citizens United? With the Supreme Court handing out unprecedented powers to the Executive branch like cake at a birthday party, and our Democratic members of Congress offering little more than strong rebukes, it often feels hopeless to reclaim lost ground. But while MAGA twists the rule of law into an unrecognizable pretzel, [Montana](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011e8Y4sY7Nji4F3itz0owJQXZCdf-4nX2XR21uOFhBiUey5Dg-zkIE4b_eYNEF03Ghh-QNU58OcgACQWHcAPgD7cquWgZDuXCi95XM8oJrrVCItJxkD72JEKgXvXfT1I9DORgshRexWBIcAlpbcdwd8meacv16FzzwGbpl30fYm0=&c=N-fjMXZIFcDXgRHRIlXvUTi1-xvGjuZomK5puih9RFXFyVTBqLT2eQ==&ch=kY30otek5Psn0qqJlA9dZWNUiMk1Be9LlTP5J2ZZ-j1SCMoGtDaSSA==) may have found a way to put real teeth into trimming back the rampant oligarchic control of our government.
Could it really be that easy? Anyone who has ever started a business knows that the first step is registering with a state. It does not have to be the state where you live, but it is at the state level that every business in the United States begins. Whether a single owner, partnership, LLC, non profit, or PAC, it all starts with state registration. From there, everyone must answer to the IRS, but depending on the type of business, additional federal filings may be required, such as with the Securities and Exchange Commission for finance or the Federal Election Commission for partisan federal elections. It is state authority that governs almost all of the rights and powers granted to a business. And this state authority is the key to undoing Citizens United.
In Montana, of all places, this idea has taken hold under the name [Transparent Election Initiative](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011e8Y4sY7Nji4F3itz0owJQXZCdf-4nX2XR21uOFhBiUey5Dg-zkIE4b_eYNEF03Ghh-QNU58OcgACQWHcAPgD7cquWgZDuXCi95XM8oJrrVCItJxkD72JEKgXvXfT1I9DORgshRexWBIcAlpbcdwd5PEEx8gU0nFUX7iVvEVAbg=&c=N-fjMXZIFcDXgRHRIlXvUTi1-xvGjuZomK5puih9RFXFyVTBqLT2eQ==&ch=kY30otek5Psn0qqJlA9dZWNUiMk1Be9LlTP5J2ZZ-j1SCMoGtDaSSA==). The initiative is so clean in its design that it would be nearly impossible even for our MAGA friendly Supreme Court to overturn. [Harvard Law](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011e8Y4sY7Nji4F3itz0owJQXZCdf-4nX2XR21uOFhBiUey5Dg-zkIE4b_eYNEF03GSMmTc9BfyvE0BnjEooAW57GZk65in-DilbUEHWChyOEiMN3cIRwVS80xAKYKdE6BkN4tn5cUuUiUF-qE-8DTOd0Sc2iwehvzAgmR79ukNVDeJuR-Cj0GwoxbgSG26Lkb1KI7UcBxqIFSvWXkOIy5FZAaObPTF0L_QTHiHcrE8QE=&c=N-fjMXZIFcDXgRHRIlXvUTi1-xvGjuZomK5puih9RFXFyVTBqLT2eQ==&ch=kY30otek5Psn0qqJlA9dZWNUiMk1Be9LlTP5J2ZZ-j1SCMoGtDaSSA==) weighed in on the subject. States rights in corporate governance are reinforced by hundreds of years of legal precedent. For the Supreme Court to overturn that doctrine would completely upend virtually every aspect of commerce and finance in this country. A real debacle. Of course, [opposition exists](https://zmhksxhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0011e8Y4sY7Nji4F3itz0owJQXZCdf-4nX2XR21uOFhBiUey5Dg-zkIE4b_eYNEF03GNxwhQ0cWCadSlNGDXb5UgzyCnq0OIbJl_oiJkq1QdoMbfwKd0q9i556ESO2NxJxxHDlWVddqGpJc6V_NMKYsxhUTRsrY9rulgdcZh7tUzUyEmxbyZkStc0Tv3BmDF_xygv4clCLKBkJOVB68bVgsCY2Z5JS_ezze73y6x2yfpqxszW8e81_KrIqWshsv3fstTS6Hxadpru0=&c=N-fjMXZIFcDXgRHRIlXvUTi1-xvGjuZomK5puih9RFXFyVTBqLT2eQ==&ch=kY30otek5Psn0qqJlA9dZWNUiMk1Be9LlTP5J2ZZ-j1SCMoGtDaSSA==), but it focuses on specific wording in the initiative, not the underlying concept.

|
Is there a downside? Yes, and it mostly affects 501(c)(4) non profits. This designation allows non profits to engage in political activity, including spending up to forty nine percent of their budget on partisan politics. They can directly tell the public to vote for or against a candidate or a ballot initiative. Under the Transparent Election Initiative, 501(c)(4) corporations would lose the right to engage in partisan political activity. So where does that leave us? Surprisingly, with more room than it first appears.
Political Action Committees are also corporations registered with the state, and therefore subject to state governance. In the Montana version of the Transparent Election Initiative, PACs are exempted, meaning they would retain the ability to engage in partisan politics, though without a tax exemption. Also, the line between partisan and non partisan political speech remains wide and usable.
In practice, what you can say in advertising is only lightly restricted. It is far more likely that media platforms such as Facebook, radio, television, or newspapers will act as stronger censors than the Federal Election Commission, which oversees federal political messaging by 501(c)(4) organizations.
If there is still a large gap in keeping big money out of partisan politics, is the Transparent Election Initiative still worth pursuing? Absolutely. It restricts businesses that exist for commerce to activities consistent with that purpose. And if an organization wants to engage in politics, it requires a separate corporate structure created specifically for that purpose, which increases transparency.

In the 2025 General Election, turnout struggled most in Franklin and Yakima counties \-- also Washington State's most Hispanic districts.
That's not a coincidence. Especially in local elections, turnout struggles significantly among Hispanic voters. Estimates using voter names and location -- a statistical model of likely voter race -- indicate that only 14.5% of likely Hispanic voters returned a ballot, compared to 36.7% overall. Likely Native American voters also had very low turnout (17.5%). While turnout was higher among identified African-American (21.9%) and Asian (23.0%), it was much less than voters modeled as likely Caucasian (40.3%).
This aligns with broader trends in local elections across the country. While socioeconomic factors like income certainly play a role, they are deeply intertwined with race, and race remains a distinct driver of turnout on its own. We see repeatedly that 'participation gaps' widen in off-cycle elections specifically for communities of color, regardless of other variables. These communities stand the most to gain electorally from fostering greater civic engagement.

This is why the work of Rural Americans United is essential. When turnout collapses among Hispanic, and Native communities, the political power of rural Washington collapses with it, leaving our democracy less representative and the most affected voices pushed further to the margins. Rural Americans United exists to reverse that trend through voter education, targeted outreach, and pro democracy communication that narrows the participation gap and ensures every rural voter is seen, heard, and empowered.

# **Erika Kirk fires back against wild conspiracy theories about her jewelry ...**
Charlie's widow Erika, who has taken over as CEO of Turning Point USA, has been forced to **[deflect rampant conspiracy theories](https://substack.com/redirect/bce89ad4-1422-4dde-862d-6d6c4dea4bed?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** including wild allegations about her jewelry, sarcastically calling them "the conspiracy collection--get it before Christmas" while flashing her bedazzled hand on Fox News' "Outnumbered," expressing "righteous anger" that the theories have attacked her family and colleagues, calling it "not OK, not healthy, a mind virus."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0d55d53b-e21a-4363-bc50-da8f695c101d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Robinson to make first in-person court appearance Thursday:** Alleged gunman Tyler Robinson, accused of killing Turning Point USA co-founder Charlie Kirk at a Utah Valley University event, will appear in person in court in Provo, Utah, on Thursday--more than three months after the caught-on-camera slaying--charged with aggravated murder, felony discharge of a firearm, obstruction of justice, two counts of witness tampering, and committing a violent offense in the presence of a child.
* **Judge weighing media access concerns for fair trial:** Both Robinson's legal team and the Utah County Sheriff's Office have requested cameras be banned from the courthouse over concerns about ensuring a fair trial, according to ABC News, with Robinson having previously appeared in court only twice--once virtually and once audio-only--and not yet having entered a plea.

# **Leaked document allegedly shows Trump 's plans to make Europe great again**
A US defense website, Defense One, claims to have seen a leaked document revealing a "Make Europe Great Again" strategy where Trump intends to pull Austria, Italy, Hungary, and Poland away from the EU and closer to Washington's influence, while backing parties that "seek sovereignty and preservation/restoration of traditional European ways of life," **[the Daily Mail reports.](https://substack.com/redirect/f1b18309-d8f9-4d7b-8da2-4f82e72971e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

---|---|---
* **White House vehemently denies leak as European alarm spreads:** White House Deputy Press Secretary Anna Kelly dismissed the claims outright, stating "President Trump is transparent and has signed a national security strategy that clearly directs the US government," while rejecting the existence of any "alternative version," though the leak triggered widespread alarm among European media and spiraled across social platforms.
* **Official strategy accuses EU of "civilizational erasure" through migration:** Trump's 33-page National Security Strategy sparked debate for warning that Europe faces "civilizational erasure" and questioning whether certain European countries will "remain reliable allies," accusing the EU of eroding sovereignty through migration policies that are "transforming the continent and creating strife" while "undermining political liberty."
* **European leaders react with fury and defiance:** European Council President Antonio Costa rebuked the US, declaring "The United States cannot replace European citizens in choosing which are the right parties," while Polish PM Donald Tusk appealed to "Dear American friends" that "Europe is your closest ally, not your problem," though Dutch hard-right politician Geert Wilders welcomed Trump's stance, saying "President Trump speaks the truth" about Europe's immigration issues.

# **Senate Republicans accuse Democrats of manufacturing healthcare crisis**
Senate Republicans are claiming that Democrats' commitment to extending Obamacare subsidies represents a **[manufactured affordability crisis](https://substack.com/redirect/58caf0e7-d893-4f6c-badb-40532057ba1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** designed to weaponize healthcare heading into 2026 midterm elections.
* **Competing proposals clash:** Minority Leader Chuck Schumer warned of "sticker shock" if Biden-era credits expire, calling Democrats' three-year extension "the last train out of this station," while GOP Senators Bill Cassidy and Mike Crapo countered with health savings accounts replacing subsidies.
* **Political motives alleged:** Senator Roger Marshall told Fox News Digital that Democrats "politically embrace this affordability issue" but their three-year extension request "does nothing but throw gasoline on the fire."
* **Deeper criticisms emerge:** Majority Whip John Barrasso argued Obamacare "has always been pricey" and Democrats want to funnel $83 billion in taxpayer money directly to insurance companies, while Senator Eric Schmitt called healthcare "an ongoing train wreck since Obamacare."

**Marshall Plan:** Senator Roger Marshall proposed the eponymous "Marshall Plan" combining one-year subsidy extension with Republican HSA demands as a potential compromise, though Republicans contend Schumer is blocking cross-aisle negotiations.

# **Trump unveils "gold card" visa program selling US residency**
The Trump administration launched its **["gold card"](https://substack.com/redirect/ba708606-1b32-4fe3-bd72-7d2506ae5d3c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** initiative Tuesday, allowing wealthy foreigners to **[purchase instant permanent residency](https://substack.com/redirect/c1733db8-9544-4ba4-9aca-304faaa64417?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for $1 million individually or $2 million for companies seeking to retain employees.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/951d8d76-efc4-4a14-975e-c4a9bb1779b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Fast-track citizenship path:** The card functions "somewhat like a green card" according to Trump, granting immediate, permanent residency eligibility with Department of Homeland Security background checks required, while holders can apply for full citizenship after five years of residence.
* **EB-5 program overhaul:** The initiative revamps the backlogged EB-5 visa system that had 250,000 foreigners waiting for approval as of February, replacing varied regional investment thresholds and job creation requirements--which issued just 135,518 visas over 25 years--with flat-rate purchases through direct Treasury payments.
* **Budget deficit strategy:** Trump expects "hundreds of billions of dollars" in revenue with support from business leaders like Apple's Tim Cook, while Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick previously calculated that 200,000 gold cards at the original $5 million price tag would generate $1 trillion toward reducing the nation's $38 trillion debt.

# Louisiana Democrat's dirty (not so) little secret...
Democratic Representative Cleo Fields purchased between $500,000 and $1.25 million in **[Netflix shares](https://substack.com/redirect/dd4a99c4-b7a2-495c-94fa-22cbc96b9ead?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ... just weeks before the streaming company announced its $82.7 billion Warner Bros acquisition.
* **Suspicious timing:** Fields executed five transactions valued at $100,001 to $250,000 each between October 31 and November 20.
* **Broader investment activity:** The Louisiana congressman simultaneously invested in Apple, Alphabet, and Nvidia during the same timeframe, making him the sole representative disclosing Netflix purchases within the past month, while GOP Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain conducted smaller Netflix trades from her 401(k) in late October.
* **Stock ban push intensifies:** The revelations surface as Representative Anna Paulina Luna advances a bipartisan discharge petition to force a congressional stock trading ban vote without leadership approval, though she remains short of 218 signatures needed.
* **Ongoing battle:** Paramount is lobbying the Trump administration and Justice Department to block the Warner Bros deal, contributing to Wall Street concerns about a potential bidding war that has driven down Netflix's share price since Fields' purchases.

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

Susie Wiles, the first female White House Chief of Staff in American history, rarely does interviews - but she made an exception for The Mom View. In this exclusive conversation, Susie opens up about her faith, her family, taking 11 years off to raise her daughters, and what it's really like to work alongside President Trump. From growing up as the daughter of NFL legend Pat Summerall to running the most consequential presidential campaign in modern history, Susie shares the untold story of her journey to the top - and why she believes motherhood is still the most important job she's ever had. All children with physical, developmental or cognitive disabilities receive at least some services through Medicaid, and Trump wants to end those services Trump’s Big Ugly Budget includes nearly **$1 trillion in cuts to Medicaid** , which funds services to disabled children, including speech, occupational and physical therapy, wheelchairs, in-home aides and medical care. If it couldn’t get any worse, Trump has gutted the Office of Civil Rights at the Department of Education. This is the main agency that enforces the 50-year-old law granting students with disabilities the right to attend school and receive an education appropriate to their needs. Before that law was enacted, students with disabilities often didn’t attend school at all. **We need to stand up for nearly 1 in 6 U.S. children who have a RIGHT to life-saving services and an education.** Able Dems is committed to electing Democrats with disabilities and our allies who will FLIP Congress, STAND up for those with disabilities and STOP these Trump cuts happening to Medicaid and the Department of Education. subject: BREAKING: Justice Democrats endorses Nida Allam in NC-04!
disclaimer_text: paid for by corporate PACs
body:
[1]Justice Democrats

BREAKING, Peter:

Today, Justice Democrats is proud to announce our seventh 2026 Democratic
primary endorsement: Nida Allam in North Carolina’s 4th district!

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251211-na.mg-emu&refcode=em20251211-37269&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1002&akid=37269%2E1203867%2EIduisl ]A graphic with a picture of Nida Allam and text reading 'Endorsement;
Nida Allam for U.S. Congress, NC-04. Join Us 2026'. There is a Justice
Democrats logo at the bottom.

Nida is the 31-year-old Durham County Commissioner who has delivered real
relief for working families in NC — and she knows how to build on that
progress in Congress. That starts by taking this seat back from AIPAC and
Crypto billionaires who bought it in 2022.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251211-na.mg-emu&refcode=em20251211-37269&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1003&akid=37269%2E1203867%2EIduisl ]Rush $5 or more to become a founding donor of her
campaign now →

The daughter of Indian and Pakistani immigrants, Nida experienced the
tragic loss of her best friend in the 2015 anti-Muslim Chapel Hill
shooting. But she turned her grief into action.

Nida organized for Bernie in college then became his NC political director
in 2016 before becoming the first Muslim woman in her state to serve in
public office when she was elected to the Durham County Board of
Commissioners in 2020.

Since making history and stepping into this role, she turned her
community’s progressive hopes into real results by:

* Passing the largest investment (over $450 million) for public schools
in Durham’s history;
* Bringing back billions in investment to create thousands of jobs in
the County that pay a living wage and don’t all require college
degrees;
* Raising the minimum wage for County and public school workers;
* Funding a homeowner relief program to support low-income families;
* Investing millions of dollars in affordable housing and mental
healthcare access;
* Building the first immigrant and refugee services program in the South
to provide support and resources to families;
* Funding the Board of Elections to provide free IDs for voters who need
them and investing in new technology to give every voter in the county
all the information they need to vote in one place.

When establishment Democrats try to dismiss our movement’s agenda for the
people as too hard or too bold — Nida is here to tell them those are
excuses paid for by corporate PACs.

With healthcare costs skyrocketing, she won’t just vote to protect our
existing care — she’ll fight to expand it by passing Medicare for All to
ensure everyone has the care they need. Not take corporate checks from the
very PACs lobbying against it.

Nida will fight to make life more affordable for everyday people by taking
on big utility corporations like Duke Energy that keep raising our energy
costs. Unlike her establishment opponent, Nida doesn’t take a dime of
corporate PAC money and will fiercely fight back against the corporations
raising our prices and making life harder for the working class.

And while AIPAC has made too many politicians too cowardly to speak up,
Nida has been a vocal opponent of the genocide in Gaza and will oppose
sending any more taxpayer dollars to Israel for bombs and weapons, and
demand that money be used to fund our communities at home.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251211-na.mg-emu&refcode=em20251211-37269&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1004&akid=37269%2E1203867%2EIduisl ]We can deliver more progress for Durham, beat AIPAC’s candidate, and
make Nida the next Justice Democrat in Congress, but only with enough
grassroots support from progressives like you. Will you pitch in any
amount to directly support Nida’s campaign from Day 1?

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20251211-na.mg-emu&refcode=em20251211-37269&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=1023&akid=37269%2E1203867%2EIduisl ]Contribute $5

In solidarity,

Alexandra Rojas
Executive Director

Contribute to Justice Democrats: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/justicedemocrats?refcode=em20251211-37269-footer&t=1024&refcode2=37269_1203867_Iduisl&akid=37269%2E1203867%2EIduisl

This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way for us to reach you about opportunities to get involved. How strong we start in January depends directly on what we can raise now. body:
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/PNG%202023%20TOP%20Newsletter%20Header.png]
Lea el boletín en español abajo [#Español]
NEXT WEEK:
Learn about TOP's latest Right2Justice efforts in Harris County
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Gave%20and%20Lady%20Justice.jpg]
We as community members have the collective power to shape policies impacting policing and our local justice systems.
We can shift away from harmful measures that prioritize punishment, leading to mass incarceration, and instead adopt restorative practices that center our humanity and allow more people to thrive.
If you're a Harris County resident interested in learning more about this latest TOP Right2Justice effort and how you can plug in, email Dr. Doshie Piper at dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] to get details on next week’s events.
SIGN UP SOON:
Healthcare Marketplace open enrollment deadlines are coming up
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Family%20healthcare%20stock.jpeg]
While this year's open enrollment period has brought with it uncertainty and confusion for the more than 24 million people who buy health insurance through the federal and state Affordable Care Act marketplaces, there are still steps marketplace shoppers can take to ensure they make informed choices for the upcoming plan year.
TOP believes healthcare is a human right, and while some elected officials (we're looking at you, Congressional Republicans) choose to play politics with this, the need to share vital healthcare information with our fellow community members has never been greater.
In most states (including Texas), people must enroll by Dec. 15 for coverage starting Jan. 1, and by Jan. 15 for coverage starting Feb. 1.
https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan [https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan]
Wishing you and your loved ones a safe and joyous holiday season
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2025%20Galveston%20mural.jpg]
This will be our last newsletter for 2025! With the continued support of members and supporters like you, we know we can keep showing up for our communities, so we can keep pushing for the positive, transformative change ALL Texans deserve — no matter our age, race, faith, spoken language, or gender.
We thank you for helping drive our efforts this year, whether that be showing up to a rally, attending a workshop, or even joining us in contacting your elected leaders. We wish you and your loved ones a joyful holiday season and new year centered in rejuvenation and fellowship.
TOP offices will be closed December 23 through January 1, as we take a moment to rest, reflect, and prepare for a busy 2026 filled with opportunities to mobilize more Texans and make more change.
TOP Tip: Consider alternatives to Amazon for your holiday shopping
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Amazon%20mailbox.jpg]
Hey, we’ve all bought goods off Amazon at some point. While the prices and fast shipping can be tempting, it's worth considering other websites for everyday products and gifts — especially if you're looking to support small businesses and be a more socially conscious shopper. Check out these alternatives! [https://www.goodgoodgood.co/articles/alternatives-to-amazon]
Español
LA PRÓXIMA SEMANA:
Infórmese sobre las últimas iniciativas de Right2Justice de TOP en el condado de Harris
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Gave%20and%20Lady%20Justice.jpg]
Como miembros de la comunidad, tenemos el poder colectivo para influir en las políticas que afectan a la policía y a nuestros sistemas de justicia locales.
Podemos alejarnos de medidas dañinas que priorizan el castigo y que llevan a un encarcelamiento masivo, y adoptar prácticas restaurativas que pongan al centro nuestra humanidad y permitan que más personas prosperen.
Si usted reside en el condado de Harris y está interesado en obtener más información sobre esta iniciativa de TOP Right2Justice y cómo puede participar, envíe un correo electrónico a la Dra. Doshie Piper a dpiper@organizetexas.org [dpiper@organizetexas.org] para obtener detalles sobre los eventos de la próxima semana.
INSCRÍBASE PRONTO:
Se acercan las fechas límite para la inscripción en el Mercado de Seguros Médicos
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Family%20healthcare%20stock.jpeg]
Aunque el período de inscripción abierta de este año ha traído incertidumbre y confusión para más de 24 millones de personas que compran seguro médico a través de los mercados estatales y federales de la Ley del Cuidado de Salud a Bajo Precio, todavía hay pasos que los compradores pueden tomar para asegurarse de tomar decisiones informadas para el próximo año del plan.
TOP cree que la atención médica es un derecho humano, y aunque algunos funcionarios electos (nos referimos a ustedes, republicanos del Congreso) optan por politizar este tema, la necesidad de compartir información vital sobre atención médica con los miembros de nuestra comunidad nunca ha sido mayor.
En la mayoría de los estados (incluido Texas), las personas deben inscribirse antes del 15 de diciembre para que su cobertura comience el 1 de enero, y antes del 15 de enero para que la cobertura comience el 1 de febrero.
https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan [https://health.usnews.com/wellness/articles/how-to-pick-a-health-insurance-plan]
Les deseamos a usted y a sus seres querido unas fiestas seguras y llenas de alegría
[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/2025%20Galveston%20mural.jpg]
¡Este será nuestro último boletín de 2025! Con el apoyo continuo de miembros y aliados como tú, sabemos que podemos seguir presentes para nuestras comunidades y seguir impulsando el cambio positivo y transformador que TODOS los texanos merecen, sin importar nuestra edad, raza, fe, idioma o género.
Te agradecemos por contribuir a nuestros esfuerzos este año, ya sea participando en una manifestación, asistiendo a un taller o incluso uniéndote a nosotros para contactar a tus representantes electos. Te deseamos a ti y a tus seres queridos una temporada festiva y un nuevo año lleno de alegría, renovación y convivencia.
Las oficinas de TOP estarán cerradas del 23 de diciembre al 1 de enero, mientras tomamos un momento para descansar, reflexionar y prepararnos para un 2026 lleno de oportunidades para movilizar a más texanos y lograr más cambios.

[https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/TSM/TSMTO/1/45640/images/Amazon%20mailbox.jpg]

I wanted to let you know that we've received several messages about the donation link and appreciate you letting us know! The issue has been fixed.

Other than that glitch, this has been an inspiring and productive week of interviewing clerks at the Alaska Association of Municipal Clerks meeting, and today we’ll be filming at the Alaska Municipal League's Local Government Conference. Your support helps us share these essential stories through ClerkStart and related programming.

Thank you for helping with this important project by donating [here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/121075568/588274641/-412970717?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGRjMmZjYS1iMGQ2LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=igNHltj7GnXSg_X6yh-mfFOTltF5ckP9lSFR9BS6kx8=&emci=e6c48482-a8d6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=e8dc2fca-b0d6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=9512399).

Veronica and Team Build Alaska’s Future
---
| | |
---
| | Happy Local Government Week in Alaska! Having just wrapped up the **60th Annual Alaska Association of Municipal Clerks Conference** , alongside several affiliate professional gatherings, today is the launch of the **Alaska Municipal League’s 75th Anniversary Annual Conference**. This week offers a rare moment to honor and elevate the people who keep Alaska’s communities functioning every single day. Across more than 230 communities, municipal and tribal local government professionals form the foundation of civic life. And among them, clerks are the heartbeat of our institutions. They run elections, safeguard public records, support councils and assemblies, maintain transparency, and provide continuity in communities facing significant demographic and workforce challenges. Alaska depends on these public servants far more than most residents ever see. To help Alaskans better understand and appreciate this vital profession, [Build Alaska’s Future Education Fund](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/121075569/588274642/-1512324198?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAxNi8xLzEwMjc1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlOGRjMmZjYS1iMGQ2LWYwMTEtODE5NS0wMDBkM2ExZDU4YWEiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=igNHltj7GnXSg_X6yh-mfFOTltF5ckP9lSFR9BS6kx8=&emci=e6c48482-a8d6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&emdi=e8dc2fca-b0d6-f011-8195-000d3a1d58aa&ceid=9512399) created **ClerkStart** , a storytelling initiative designed to elevate local government roles and inspire the next generation of civic leaders. **This week, in celebration of Local Government Week, we are on the ground at both AAMC and AML interviewing and filming clerks and other local government officials** for a high-quality, five-minute video spotlight. Their experiences, insights, and deep pride in serving their communities are at the center of this work. Derek, we know it’s the holiday season, and everyone is busy — but we’re hoping you take just a minute out of your day to hear us out. We wanted to share three reasons to give to the DNC today:
1️⃣ Democrats’ big wins this year were only possible because people chipped in early and often — allowing us to distribute funds and resources to the campaigns and organizations that needed them most.

2️⃣ Trump’s agenda is historically unpopular, and we have a real chance to win the House and Senate to prevent more damage and destruction. But to do it, we need to deliver victories in states and districts Democrats haven’t won in decades. We don’t say this to scare you — it’s the truth. And we _know_ we can win in places that have felt out of reach when we all work together.

3️⃣ Winning these majorities will be hard work and will require even stronger infrastructure than what we built in 2025. There are experts, organizers, and volunteers right now working day in and day out across the country to build that foundation — but they need your help.
