Hi, folks – Michael here. This is going to be a longer email, but I need you to read every word of it:
After 43 days, the longest government shutdown in U.S. history ended with the Republican Senate majority leader promising to hold a vote on a clean extension of Obamacare (or Affordable Care Act) subsidies, to keep working folks' health premiums within reach.
**That vote was today. I was in favor – but all except four of my Republican colleagues voted to kill it. They succeeded.**
So now, over 24 million Americans – including nearly 300,000 in Colorado – will pay double, triple, or even quadruple for their health insurance premiums in the new year.
That's thousands upon thousands more dollars, and it's coming at a time when countless regular working families are already struggling to put food on the table, let alone put a few gifts for the kids under the tree. **Most folks just don't have that kind of money.**
Between the end of ACA subsidies and Trump's Big, Bad Betrayal of a Bill strangling Medicaid in a wall of red tape, roughly 15 MILLION folks nationwide are expected to lose access to lifesaving health care.
_That's_ the reality of Trump and the GOP's failed leadership: working families forced to choose between going to the doctor and bankruptcy ... **all so billionaires like Trump himself can enjoy TRILLIONS more in tax cuts.** I wish I were joking.
It's also a big part of why I'm running to bring the fight for you back home in the first place – because the best fixes to the issues facing Colorado _cannot_ and _will not_ come from the broken politics of Trump's party. Since they control Washington, the most effective pushback to Trump's agenda will come from the states.
**As governor, I promise I'll fight like hell to protect affordable health care access in Colorado, even as national Republicans hang us out to dry. **
But to follow through on this, I'll first need the resources to win this race. Hitting my final $20,000 mid-month goal of the year by this Monday’s deadline is key – and I don't stand a chance of reaching it without you, friend.
**So if you're in a place where you can give today, I'm humbly asking you to follow the link below to pitch in $5, or anything you can now, to help me bring home the fight as our next governor.** Together, I know we have what it takes to win this race and build a brighter future for every Coloradan – not just the wealthy few.

Peter,
While you were likely worrying about affording heating bills or buying gifts for your family, Lauren Boebert was in D.C. partying at what can only be described as the Christmas Party from Hell.
She wasn't hearing from her constituents in Colorado (she still hasn't shown up in person for a town hall). She was rubbing elbows at a bash hosted by disgraced, expelled former Congressman George Santos.
And look at the guest list. It reads like a "Who's Who" of grifters and extremists:

But this isn't the only unsavory company she keeps.
While she attended the Christmas party, a scandal was unfolding: Reports now indicate Boebert is facing potential campaign finance violations for allegedly using campaign funds to pay thousands of dollars to see her alleged lover, Kid Rock.
The same Kid Rock who used racial slurs and waved a handgun at a journalist in a Rolling Stone interview just last year, and a man who regularly performs on stage with the Confederate flag as a backdrop.
Fraudsters. Racists. Disgraced liars. This is Lauren Boebert's inner circle.
She treats her seat like a VIP pass to the worst party on earth, but that's made her more vulnerable than ever. She's only in Congress because of 546 votes, raised five times less than us last quarter, and last time Democrat Trisha Calvarese ran against her, she had the best performance of any Democrat in the district's history.
[Elections this year have proven even deep red seats can be flipped by Dems, and CO-4 is a prime target in '26\. We have the momentum to end this national embarrassment. | | Hi Fellow Patriot,

My name is Lauren Toncich -- and for the past seven years, I've helped lead the team behind the curtain at every Turning Point USA event.

Making sure the lights hit at the right moment, the music is pumping through the crowd, and tens of thousands of people walk into something unforgettable.

I've never emailed you directly before.

But if you've ever seen the opening night of AmericaFest... felt the electricity of a Student Action Summit crowd... or watched one of our massive rallies ignite a room...

Then you've witnessed the kind of energy Charlie dreamed of -- brought to life by our incredible events team.

At the heart of every single Turning Point event is this one truth: _Young Americans deserve a stage worthy of the fight they 're in. _

**And AmericaFest -- especially this year -- is our most important stage of all. **

**This December 18 -21 in Phoenix, thousands of students will walk into the most powerful conservative gathering in America. **

It will be our first AmFest without Charlie.

This is the stage he built -- with vision, grit, and sky-high standards.

Charlie poured everything into these events, because he believed students deserved more than beige ballrooms and lazy lectures.

He believed they needed to _FEEL_ the mission -- That they were part of something unstoppable... something big enough to change the world.

Backstage, I can still hear him directing the show: _" Louder music... more sparks... bigger energy... how full are we looking?" _

Not because he wanted flash for the sake of flash...

But because he knew energy moves people. Environments shape conviction.

_And atmosphere matters when you 're calling students into the fight of their lives. _

This year's AmFest?

_I 've never seen more students eager to be part of it. _

**Nearly 6,000 are registered. Another 2,200 are on the waitlist. **

**And we only have a few days left to get them in. **

Fellow Patriot, these students aren't looking for entertainment...

They're looking for courage, purpose, and a movement to belong to.

They're stepping onto hostile campuses. They're getting flak from Leftist professors.

Many are leading Turning Point chapters in places where they're told to sit down, shut up -- or worse.

**They want to stand for America... _They just need a chance to stand with others who will, too. _**

And when they get to AmFest, it's not just the main stage that changes their lives.

Behind the lights and cameras, they sit in smaller breakout rooms -- face-to-face with staff and speakers who show them exactly how to lead.

Students walk in with doubts, with fears, with barely enough money to afford the flight.

They walk out with confidence, connection, and a new sense of calling.

I've seen them go home and start chapters. I've seen them run for office.

Many tell me -- even years later, that this one event changed everything.

_So no -- I'm not just asking you to sponsor an "event." _

**I 'm asking you to help change the trajectory of a young patriot. **

Fellow Patriot, I know what Charlie would want right now.

He'd want every seat filled. He'd want AmFest to echo with boldness and fire.

He'd want us to fight like he's still backstage -- still calling for more sparks.

Most of all, he'd want every student who made the trip to believe they were part of something bigger than themselves.

To walk in searching for purpose -- and leave filled with it. .

Let's make sure every young patriot who wants to fight for this country gets their chance -- and gets to Phoenix this December.

Making sure the lights hit at the right moment, the music is pumping through the crowd, and tens of thousands of people walk into something unforgettable. I've never emailed you directly before. #
Demand Justice just launched **No Crony Judges** , a major new campaign that draws a bright line for Democrats: any Senator who claims to defend democracy must vote NO on Trump’s dishonest judicial nominees.
The facts about Trump’s nominees are brutal:
* 0 nominees admit Joe Biden won in 2020.
* 0 nominees tell the truth about January 6 — 21 of 27 call it a “political issue.”

And yet: **18 Democratic Senators** — Coons, Durbin, Fetterman, Gallego, Hassan, Heinrich, Kaine, Kelly, King, Klobuchar, Hirono, Peters, Reed, Rosen, Schiff, Shaheen, Welch, and Whitehouse — have already confirmed at least one.
[**Add your name now to join Demand Justice in holding lawmakers accountable for their judicial confirmation votes.**](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22114?t=1&akid=1399%2E2118727%2EfeTDHH)

**Our No Crony Judges campaign makes it clear: Senate Democrats must vote NO on every Trump nominee peddling his agenda and stand up for independent courts, or be held accountable.**

Earlier this year, the Wisconsin Supreme Court rejected a 176-year-old abortion ban, safeguarding reproductive healthcare access for our state.
Recently, our far-right opponent, Maria Lazar, was asked about her position on this ruling.
Lazar’s response? _“I don’t know that I would've been in the majority on that case.”_
Wisconsinites deserve judges who will protect our freedoms — not question them.
That’s the difference in this race: **Maria Lazar would threaten our fundamental rights. Judge Chris Taylor will defend them.**
But values alone won’t win this race.
Right-wing special interests could start spending millions to boost Lazar’s campaign without warning, and we’re counting on grassroots support to fight back and win. [**Will you chip in $10 to elect Judge Chris Taylor?**](https://act.chrisforjustice.com/go/31?c0=em_ms_jct_20251211_1_ak.b87jHP&amount=10&refcode=em20251211-904&t=3&akid=905%2E294397%2EZDCoQD)

| | Derek,

**I NEVER thought I'd say it: **
**I just had a great day on Beacon Hill. **
The Massachusetts State House is lovely this time of year, and we came bearing gifts and a good message: **New Hampshire Can't Afford to Lose Maura Healey.**
---

It's a simple message. On tax after tax, New Hampshire outperforms Massachusetts and it's time we let the Massachusetts business community - and their residents - know about.
At the press conference, I laid out exactly why companies like Analogic and SynQor are leaving Massachusetts and choosing Salem for their future. This is not luck. It is the direct result of smart policy, disciplined leadership, and a town that refuses to stand in the way of growth.
I reminded the press that every time Massachusetts adds another tax or regulation, New Hampshire becomes even more attractive. We are not rooting for Massachusetts to fail. We are focused on New Hampshire succeeding. When they push employers out, we welcome them in. That is why two major global companies just chose Salem and why more are already looking our way.
Now that I've gone into the Massachusetts' liberal den to speak the truth, I know the left will be throwing everything they can to turn New Hampshire into Massachusetts-lite. _**We cannot let that happen!**_
I want you to join me in this fight and to help emphasis how strong our New Hampshire Advantage is.

subject: National Republicans are failing us
body:
The GOP’s one-party rule has to end.
|

_I’m not afraid to call it like I see it, Peter._ Republicans in Washington are targeting their political opponents for persecution. While Trump is calling for the execution of American leaders like Senators Mark Kelly and Elissa Slotkin, his Justice Department is fomenting phony investigations that destroy trust in our judicial system and end up wasting American taxpayers' money. Meanwhile, the GOP is creating financial devastation for everyday Americans while claiming that prices are down and ripping away health care because their wealthy donors wanted a tax cut. **Every manufactured crisis, every attack on their enemies — it’s all designed to distract the people from the real harm they are causing.** Their policies are going to destroy this country if we let them. _But not if I have anything to say about it._ **[Can I count on you to join me in the fight, Peter? Republicans see me as their top threat, and they're committed to spending _hundreds of millions of dollars_ to defeat me. I’m supporting Mandela Barnes for Governor
| [](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-dec25.SSbw4W&amount=15&refcode=SBD_MB_EM_FR_121125_LeVarBurton_Tier2_D1_S1&t=2&akid=5705%2E196590%2Ea8MEYl) Hi , LeVar Burton here. You might know me from Roots, Reading Rainbow, or Star Trek: The Next Generation. **Today, I’m more than proud to share that I'm endorsing my good friend Mandela Barnes to be the next governor of Wisconsin.** This is a critical moment in our country — no one can deny that. Mandela’s bold leadership is exactly what we need to tackle today’s problems with creative, innovative solutions. **[Will you chip in to Mandela’s campaign today?](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-dec25.SSbw4W&amount=15&refcode=SBD_MB_EM_FR_121125_LeVarBurton_Tier2_D1_S1&t=3&akid=5705%2E196590%2Ea8MEYl)** I come from a family of educators, and it has been my life’s mission to make sure that future generations have the skills to learn, grow, and be civically engaged. Education and the arts have been under constant attack by this current administration. And after hosting Reading Rainbow for more than 20 years on PBS, I was devastated to see federal funding for public broadcasting completely decimated. I believe that protecting services like these is vital. Hearing each other’s stories brings us together, fosters connection, and keeps us engaged with our communities. I know that as governor, Mandela is going to do just that. You don’t have to take my word for it — Mandela has an important story to tell. I look forward to seeing him on the campaign trail as he shares his vision for a Wisconsin where everyone can live up to their fullest potential. **[I hope you’ll join me in supporting Mandela with a contribution of $15 or $27.](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/1212?c0=mb-em-fr-dec25.SSbw4W&amount=15&refcode=SBD_MB_EM_FR_121125_LeVarBurton_Tier2_D1_S1&t=4&akid=5705%2E196590%2Ea8MEYl)** _If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process now._ | | | [DONATE $15 »](https://act.mandelabarnes.com/go/6574?amount=15&refcode=SBD_MB_EM_FR_121125_LeVarBurton_Tier2_D1_S1&t=5&akid=5705%2E196590%2Ea8MEYl)

clean_body: If we don't pick up the pace, we could lose all of our gains for 2024. | Fellow American, it's headlines like this that keep me up at night: In 2024, we flipped Senate seats in Montana, Ohio, West Virginia, and Pennsylvania - the most gains for any party in 10 years! But here's where I am worried - all of those gains could be erased if we don't step up now. Jon Tester spent nearly $70 million to lose a seat here in Montana. Democrats are NOT going to allow this to go unanswered next year. Will you help change the momentum? I am not asking for millions of dollars, nor even $100 (but if you can spare it, I would appreciate it). Last cycle, I was the architect of our new Senate majority. That's put a #1 target on my back. We cannot start 2026 behind! Thanks, Steve Daines Steve Daines is a fifth-generation Montanan, life-long sportsman and father of four serving the people of Montana as their Senator. Team, there’s a crisis going on in America right now — one that far too few are paying attention to.

**The unemployment rate among Black Women has now risen for the third month in a row. It’s soared to 7.5% — well above the 4.4% national rate.**

Economic experts have made clear that this is a crisis.

Any cracks in the strength of the overall economy always show up for Black workers first – and at a time when all of us are feeling the strain, this is a “canary in the coal mine” for the entire economy.

This crisis has everything to do with the reckless and dangerous policies of the Trump White House — from his mass federal firings to his refusal to bring down healthcare costs.

**Look, team: There are nine men named "John" in the Senate right now. There have only been five Black women elected to the Senate — ever.**

I’m proud to be one of them. Because representation matters, and our United States Senate should reflect the country it's been elected to serve.

This kind of representation is how we call out unnoticed crises like this one. It’s how resolutions like Black Women's Equal Pay Day get passed. Or how we make sure we advocate for Black maternal healthcare.

We need more women of color in the places where important decisions are being made. But here's the hard truth:

**_Black women running for office raise 1/3 of the funds that our white counterparts do. That puts us at a major disadvantage as we fight for the representation we need._**

[**I've set a midnight goal of $10,000 to help elect more Black women to office, and I need your help. name: Cori Bush
subject: Dark money just showed up in our race.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Cori For Us
body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act]
Peter,
A new dark-money group just elbowed their way into our race. In a democracy where the people choose, billionaires and corporations are doing everything they can to get their way.
They think they can play St. Louis like we won’t notice what’s really going on, but they are mistaken.
Can you chip in $10 right now to make sure we have the resources to push back? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act&amount=10]
This group calls itself the National Black Empowerment Action Fund. But here’s the truth:
There is nothing empowering about a group run by operatives who have spent decades on AIPAC’s payroll. It’s the same people who have tried again and again to silence voices like mine.
Now they’re pouring money into this race to take control away from the people.
They’re not here to “empower” voters. They’re here to manipulate our community and buy this seat for the same right-wing interests that have been attacking our progressive movement from day one.
Just look at the billboard they put up in St. Louis this week:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act]
This is the playbook:
1. Put a friendly face on a dark-money operation.
2. Pretend to speak for our community.
3. Use Republican megadonor cash to influence a Democratic primary.
They did it last election. AIPAC spent over $9 million attacking our movement and backing my opponent. Now they’re gearing up to do it again, with new front groups who won’t have our backs.
But our community is smarter than they think. St. Louis knows who stands with the people and who stands with Republican megadonors, anti-labor billionaires, and the far-right forces funding these groups.
Peter,this is exactly why we need a strong, people-powered response today [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act] .
If we don’t answer this attack now, they will define the conversation before we can even speak.
Will you rush a $10, $25, or $50 donation to help us push back against AIPAC’s dark-money groups and protect this seat for the people of St. Louis? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act&amount=25]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:

DONATE $100 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?express_lane=true&amount=100&refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act] OTHER [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/upl_cab_email-25q4?express_lane_other=true&refcode=x_251211_bellbillboard_act]
This race has never been about me. It’s about who gets to decide the future of St. Louis: the people, or the Republican megadonors who think they can buy our district’s voice.
Let’s show them our community cannot be bought.
In solidarity,
Cori Bush

Peter,
On September 2, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered commanders to kill everyone on board a small vessel in the Caribbean, according to reporting from the Washington Post [https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2025/11/28/hegseth-kill-them-all-survivors-boat-strike/] . Two unarmed survivors, who were prepared to surrender, were killed in a second strike based on Hegseth’s directive.
Now Hegseth is acting dishonorably and shifting the blame for the second strike, which amounts to a war crime, to Admiral Bradley.
I’m calling on Pete Hegseth and Admiral Bradley to testify before Congress and explain their decisions to launch this and other strikes in the Caribbean and the Pacific. These bombing campaigns were ordered without proper authorization, without consultation with Congress, and without a clear plan to protect regional stability.

name: David Hogg
subject: We’re endorsing Nida Allam for Congress
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY LEADERS WE DESERVE, LEADERSWEDESERVE
body:
Let’s show them we’re up for this fight.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20251211-1&t=1&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)
Peter, we’ve got more exciting news today:
**I’m proud to announce that Leaders We Deserve is endorsing Nida Allam for Congress in North Carolina’s 4th District.**
[](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251211_1_nida.A_LvQd&refcode=em20251211-2930&amount=5&t=2&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)
Nida is a bold, unapologetic progressive who’s shown up for her community again and again — and now she’s stepping up to run against a Democratic incumbent who’s fallen short when North Carolinians are demanding real leadership.
**[Will you split a $5 donation now to support Nida’s campaign and help us elect more young progressives like her across the country?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251211_1_nida.A_LvQd&refcode=em20251211-2930&amount=5&t=3&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)**
Since 2024, NC-04 has been hit with the steepest federal budget cuts in the country thanks to Trump’s DOGE. And while her constituents struggled, Rep. Valerie Foushee stayed silent. She failed to stand up to the administration or fight for the people she was elected to represent.
Nida is running because this moment demands urgency. She’s already made history as the first Muslim woman ever elected to office in North Carolina. As Chair of the Durham County Board of Commissioners, she’s delivered real wins: securing the largest school bond in county history, raising wages for county workers, and working to launch a guaranteed income pilot.
And this time, the political landscape has shifted. Redistricting has made the electorate more favorable for Nida — especially with the addition of thousands of AAPI voters who’ve supported her in the past.
Nida first got involved in politics and organizing after the 2015 Chapel Hill shooting, where three of her friends were murdered in an anti-Muslim hate crime that shattered her community and changed her life forever. Since then, she’s never stopped organizing. She helped lead Bernie’s 2016 campaign in multiple states, fought to elect progressive judges in North Carolina, and built a pipeline of local leaders who reflect the communities they serve.
She’s not in this for herself. She’s in this to make sure government works for her children and the people — not dark money donors or political insiders.
But we know what Nida’s up against. In 2022, Rep. Foushee benefited from massive outside spending and AIPAC-aligned super PACs, turning a safe blue seat into _one of the most expensive Democratic primaries in state history._
This race is a test of what kind of leadership we want in Congress — and whether our movement can overcome the entrenched political machines that have shut out young, progressive candidates for too long.
**[Let’s show them we’re up for the fight. Will you split $5 today to power Nida’s campaign and help Leaders We Deserve elect more young progressives across the country?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251211_1_nida.A_LvQd&refcode=em20251211-2930&amount=5&t=4&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20251211_1_nida.A_LvQd&amount=5&refcode=em20251211-2930&t=23&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)**
Thank you for being in the fight with us,
David Hogg
* * *
**[Donate »](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/lwd-em-footer?refcode=em20251211-1&t=24&refcode2=2930_587540_Cc6W-3&akid=2930%2E587540%2ECc6W-3)**

| | Dorian Gray glanced at the picture, and suddenly an uncontrollable feeling of hatred for Basil Hallward came over him, as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas, whispered into his ear by those grinning lips. The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him.

Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675*, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. The Grand Hetman of the Crown, the future King of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, Jan Sobieski, who knew Sirko well and met him in Bratslav in 1671.

The mad passions of a hunted animal stirred within him, and he loathed the man who was seated at the table, more than in his whole life he had ever loathed anything. He glanced wildly around. Something glimmered on the top of the painted chest that faced him. His eye fell on it. He knew what it was. It was a knife that he had brought up, some days before, to cut a piece of cord, and had forgotten to take away with him. He moved slowly towards it, passing Hallward as he did so. As soon as he got behind him, he seized it and turned round. Hallward stirred in his chair as if he was going to rise. He rushed at him and dug the knife into the great vein that is behind the ear, crushing the man’s head down on the table and stabbing again and again. There was a stifled groan and the horrible sound of some one choking with blood. Three times the outstretched arms shot up convulsively, waving grotesque, stiff-fingered hands in the air. He stabbed him twice more, but the man did not move. Something began to trickle on the floor. He waited for a moment, still pressing the head down. Then he threw the knife on the table, and listened. He could hear nothing, but the drip, drip on the threadbare carpet. He opened the door and went out on the landing. The house was absolutely quiet. No one was about. For a few seconds he stood bending over the balustrade and peering down into the black seething well of darkness. Then he took out the key and returned to the room, locking himself in as he did so. The thing was still seated in the chair, straining over the table with bowed head, and humped back, and long fantastic arms. Had it not been for the red jagged tear in the neck and the clotted black pool that was slowly widening on the table, one would have said that the man was simply asleep. How quickly it had all been done! He felt strangely calm, and walking over to the window, opened it and stepped out on the balcony. The wind had blown the fog away, and the sky was like a monstrous peacock’s tail, starred with myriads of golden eyes. He looked down and saw the policeman going his rounds and flashing the long beam of his lantern on the doors of the silent houses. The crimson spot of a prowling hansom gleamed at the corner and then vanished. A woman in a fluttering shawl was creeping slowly by the railings, staggering as she went. Now and then she stopped and peered back. Once, she began to sing in a hoarse voice. The policeman strolled over and said something to her. She stumbled away, laughing. A bitter blast swept across the square. The gas-lamps flickered and became blue, and the leafless trees shook their black iron branches to and fro. He shivered and went back, closing the window behind him. People who’ve seen it are rewatching and asking the same question: “If this is happening here, what else is already in motion?” Ivan Dmytrovych Sirko was born in the early seventeenth century, approximately between 1605 and 1610. This is evidenced primarily by the results of research on Sirko's remains, according to which the Cossack ataman was 70-75 years old at the time of his death in 1680. The first researcher of Sirko's biography, the famous Ukrainian historian Dmytro Yavornytskyi, suggested that the future ataman was born in Sloboda Ukraine in the settlement of Merefa (now the city of Merefa, Kharkiv region). However, this is not true. Merefa was founded only in 1658, i.e. when Sirko was in his late teens. However, Sirko and his family lived in Merefa for a long time in his house, and after his death, his wife and some family members lived there. The fact that Merefa in Slobozhanshchyna is associated with the name of the Cossack Ataman is evidenced by another name for the town recorded in some Ukrainian chronicles, Sirkivka. Where, then, should we look for Sirko's homeland? In our opinion, the sources give grounds to localize it in Eastern Podillia, namely in the Vinnytsia region. It is worth recalling that Sirko was a colonel in Vinnytsia (Kalnytsia) in 1658-1660. As you know, at that time in Ukraine, people who came from the local area were usually elected to such positions. Let us also recall a letter from Hetman of the Left Bank Ukraine Ivan Samoilovych to the tsarist voivode Prince G. Romodanovsky of April 20, 1675, which recounts (in Russian) Sirko's own words: "And since I was born among the Poles, I want to die there." Thus, it is clear that Sirko was born on the Ukrainian lands that were under the rule of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, not Muscovy (the latter included Slobozhanshchyna). The historian Volodymyr Borysenko's assumption that Sirko's birthplace was the hundred-man town of the Bratslav regiment Murafa, a few kilometers from Kalnyk, is correct. Now it is the village of Zhdanov, Vinnytsia region. By the way, Murafa in the Slobozhanshchyna probably originated from this Murafa, because immigrants from the Right Bank of Ukraine to the Left Bank often gave the newly founded settlements the names of their native villages or towns. It is also worth noting Sirko's great interest in Keleberda, which he founded in 1675 on the left bank of the Dnipro. For a long time, he sought from the Moscow tsar the right to own this town or sloboda, as well as the strategically important crossing of the Dnipro near Perevolochna (Sirko wanted this crossing not for himself, but for the entire Zaporozhian Lowland Army). Contrary to popular belief, we believe that Sirko did not come from a Cossack family, but from a small Ukrainian Orthodox gentry. For example, we know the name of a Podillia nobleman, Voytekh Sirko, who was married to a certain Olena Kozynska. Sources mention them in 1592. It is possible that they were relatives of the Cossack leader. Perhaps it is no coincidence that the kings of the Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth, writing to Sirko, called him "urodzon." The word "nobleman" evokes negative associations for many people due to stereotypes instilled in school textbooks of the Stalinist era. However, this approach is not always correct. The term "nobleman" is identical to the words "knight," "chevalier," "nobleman," etc. and was commonly used not only in Poland but also in Ukraine, Belarus, and the Czech Republic. If scholars in Russia, Poland, and the Czech Republic, having contracted vulgar sociologism, no longer accuse Pushkin or Bunin, Suvorov or Kutuzov, Žižka or Kostiushko of being of noble or gentry origin, why have attacks on the Ukrainian and Belarusian gentry continued until recently? Is it not because in this way the imperial "divide and conquer" was transferred to our long-suffering history? Was it not because it was necessary to impose a nihilistic attitude toward the history of Ukraine, to "prove" that Ukrainians or Belarusians were just dark labor without national consciousness, ethnographic material doomed to build other people's empires? Meanwhile, the Ukrainian gentry produced many outstanding sons of Ukraine, fighters for its freedom. Suffice it to mention the names of Kryshtof Kosinski, Petro Konashevych-Sahaidachny, Ivan Sulyma, Ivan Mazepa, Bohdan Khmelnytsky, and his associates: Ivan and Danylo Vyhovsky, Ivan Bohun, Danylo and Ivan Nechai, Mykhailo Krychevsky, Jan Sokolovsky, Siluyan Muzhylovsky, and others. Sirko's appearance and personality do not always coincide with the conventional ideas about him that have developed in some works of art. The Cossack leader was slightly taller than average (174-176 cm), had regular facial features, and a straight nose. By the way, the great Relin intuitively caught this when he depicted him in the center of his painting "Cossacks Writing a Letter to the Turkish Sultan." It is interesting that the prototype for Sirko's image in the painting was the famous military leader General Dragomirov. Only one significant detail was not known to Repin and his consultant D. Yavornytskyi - a red birthmark on Sirko's lower lip on the right side. His contemporaries considered it a "sign of God" given to distinguish him from ordinary people. Friend, did you get your yearly checkup?
I wish that we had Medicare for All and everyone in the United States could answer yes, but we live in a country where our elected leaders don't consider healthcare a human right.
Instead, they think that the profits of private insurers and pharmaceutical companies are more important than guaranteeing that Americans have coverage.
Honestly, it's unconscionable for our elected leaders and our opponents, one of whom is a former doctor, to not support Medicare for All.
While people skip meals to pay for lifesaving drugs, he only pretends to care by pushing for bandaid solutions to this crisis that were pre-approved by the healthcare industry— one of his biggest donors.
Friend, our healthcare system is broken, and it doesn't take a doctor to see that.
I'm running for Congress because our communities need someone in Washington that doesn't want to cut their healthcare to pay for billionaire tax cuts and won't twiddle their thumbs while people beg for progress. Heidi Hall

Today, Heidi chairs the Nevada County Board of Supervisors, where she’s taken on homelessness, expanded broadband access, and worked to reduce crime and illegal cannabis growth. Heidi flipped her seat from red to blue – and now she’s ready to do it again in Congress to take on toxic politics in Washington and put people first.

body:
[ https://act.squadvictoryfund.com/go/18910?refcode=em20251211-1704-foote&t=1001&akid=1704%2E342411%2EVGAXBn ]Squad Victory Fund

Peter,

Here are three things you need to know:

1. We don’t rely on corporate PAC money or billionaire donations. We rely
on grassroots power — people who believe in a better future for the
working-class, not the wealthy and powerful looking to buy influence.
That keeps our work fearless and accountable to the people.
2. The Squad doesn’t back down. Whether it’s speaking truth to power,
calling out corruption, standing up to authoritarianism, or tackling
the fights others ignore, the Squad has always shown up. And your
support makes sure we can keep showing up — loudly, proudly, and
without apology.
3. We’re building a nationwide people-powered movement. This isn’t just
politics as usual. This is a movement rooted in justice, equality, and
bold progressive change. A movement that believes in lifting up every
community, defending our rights, and standing with those who need us
most.

That’s who we are. That’s who this team is. And that’s the fight that
keeps our movement strong and allows us to defend our progressive
champions at every turn.

Right now, the Squad is up against the far-right and MAGA extremists
trying to silence our progress. But with your help, we can push back. We
can win the fights that matter, protect our champions, and keep building
the movement that refuses to settle for the status quo.

**You couldn't create a more opaque health care system than the one in the U.S. No one pays more for less than we do.**

And when we’re facing an urgent affordability crisis, it’s unconscionable to me that 48 of my Republican colleagues just voted against the simplest and easiest way to ensure millions of Americans don’t face skyrocketing insurance costs next year.

But let me also say this: extending the Obamacare tax credits is at best a short-term solution to a larger problem.

**It's become obvious to me that in order to have a sustainable system, we have to have universal health care, so that we don't focus only on who has coverage, but put our focus on bringing costs down for everyone.**

Folks who have known me for a while understand that I haven’t always felt that we needed universal coverage – I thought the market would solve the coverage problem – but our economy and the way we work is changing. Most Americans no longer hold the same nine-to-five job for the majority of their careers, as they have in decades past. We have seen exponential growth in people starting or working at small businesses. Many people work as contractors. Many Americans have side hustles, gigs, and second jobs to cover their bills.

However, what I have seen is that it’s time to move past the unhelpful partisan fights over coverage and pieces of the Affordable Care Act and move towards a system that cuts out the middleman, guarantees health care coverage no matter your employer, and ensures Americans are not deciding between paying for food on the table or covering their monthly premiums.

**The path forward won’t be easy. Huge systemic change like this doesn’t happen overnight. And frankly, it will require bipartisan leadership, deal-making, and consensus-building.**

It’s a tough job – but one that I am ready to lead. That’s why I am asking Virginians to rehire me for one more term in office. And I can’t win without your help.

Well my friends, every once in a while on _Amped Up_ , we get a guest who reminds me how I fell in love with politics, history and political media--and buried myself in campaign politics long before I ever thought I'd host a show of my own about it.
Today was that day.
David Shuster and I welcomed the legendary [Chris Matthews](https://open.substack.com/users/19765871-chris-matthews?utm_source=mentions) on _Amped Up_ --yes, _that_ Chris Matthews--one of the original cable news political hosts and and pundits, when facts were things that didn't have "alternative" in front of them and someone was forced to answer a question they tried to avoid while playing _Hardball_.
Before Chris even appeared on screen, we were buzzing--and no, not in a Don Jr, eyes-half-closed live stream kinda way. We were excited. David worked under Chris as a Hardball correspondent. Chris was a mentor, a teacher, the kind of newsroom leader who didn't just shape segments, but shaped careers.
And when David says he loves Chris Matthews, it's based on the fact he's forgotten more about politics than the entire Trump Administration ever knew, and did his best to impart that on those who worked with him. He was passionate about politics, not just the strategy--though that too--but as a means of improving people's lives.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27b96dfa-41e8-45a5-825e-ae5531136f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I grew up watching _Hardball_ , and if you're anything like me--someone who cares about deepy about American democracy, so I can therefor no longer stomach a minute, much less an hour of cable coverage--you know exactly how important that Chris' show was.
Chris brought something to political broadcasting that we frankly don't almost at all anymore: a combo of toughness, storytelling, humor, institutional memory, and love of the game. He knew politics because he _lived_ _it_.
This was a point I made to him about why I loved his show: He was one of just two anchors when he was on MSNBC who had worked on campaigns and in Congress--_he knew what he was talking about_ , _not from reading it in a book, from being in the trenches and making the decisions_.
He walked the halls of Congress as an aide to famous House Speaker Tip O'Neill. He wrote speeches for President Jimmy Carter. He was in these political fights before he ever sat behind a desk. And it showed--night after night, when the rest of cable news was still figuring out what it even wanted to be, _Hardball_ had already set the standard.
* * *

* * *
So when he joined us, I felt a mix of gratitude and awe. Here's a guy whose work literally shaped how millions of Americans understand politics, democracy, winning, losing, power, values--and he brought all that history, all that voice, all that fire right into our studio. His show, unlike so many today, educated people on the topic.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27b96dfa-41e8-45a5-825e-ae5531136f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
We talked with Chris about a number of topics, including the Miami mayoral earthquake, affordability, and the political realignment happening right under our feet. As always, Chris went straight to the gut-level reality of how voters think, how memory works, how short-term economic pain shifts entire electoral maps.
When he describes the price of cream cheese going from $2 to $7, _you_ _got it that he gets it_. That's Chris--taking the 50,000-foot issue and dropping it right onto the kitchen table. And damn did his bringing up Philly Cream heese make me hungry for a good raisin bagel with chive cream cheese. But I digress 😉.
We also dove into the [Caribbean boat strikes and the #DeleteGate revelations](https://substack.com/redirect/ae465faf-1036-46d3-9208-dbc82d477225?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that [Melissa Corrigan, she/her](https://open.substack.com/users/13839118-melissa-corrigan-sheher?utm_source=mentions) and David have been breaking wide open. Chris instantly jumped into the stakes--legally, morally, politically. And when he said Trump might not pay a political price for these killings because of how communities ravaged by drugs perceive the crisis, he wasn't endorsing it--_**he was diagnosing it with the clear-eyed honesty that made Hardball essential viewing**_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/76f0394e-8106-447a-9c9c-e4620024a9c6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But what I really enjoyed most was out discussion about Bobby Kennedy, the subject of Chris's new book, _Lessons from Bobby: Ten Reasons Robert F. Kennedy Still Matters_.
When Chris talks about who Bobby Kennedy was--his toughness, his compassion, his ability to unite white working-class voters and Black Americans with a singular political vision--you can tell how much he revered the man. It's like Stephen Miller talking about deportation or Pete Hegseth dreaming of his eight Dewar's.
In his book and in his voice on Amped Up, you could hear yearning for political courage, for moral clarity, for a kind of leadership from Democrats we had with Bobby Kennedy, LBJ, and other "take no sh*t Democrats" of that era. The ones the Democratic Party has some of, _but desperately needs in leadership forthwith_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/27b96dfa-41e8-45a5-825e-ae5531136f6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
That time Chris Matthews kept pushing for an answer, so turncoat former Democrat, Zell Miller, challenged him to...a duel!
It reminded me why Chris Matthews became Chris Matthews. Why _Hardball_ mattered. [How far political media has fallen](https://substack.com/redirect/38f788ef-b1e3-4b6c-99d2-0b42052adfae?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Why we still need voices who understand politics not as some abstract chess match or scholarly paper, but as a human, bruising, consequential fight for the soul of the country and lives of our people.
For me, it wasn't just a show. It was a reminder of lineage and legacy. Of what political storytelling looks like when done by someone who helped invent its form in media. There is so much more, so you definintely should watch the video--and we will be sharing clips!
But I'm grateful we got to share Chris Matthews with all of you, and, if I'm being honst, I'm grateful I got to share Chris Matthews with me. What a show!

[Bernardo Ruiz Website](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/820221b9-df2b-4ac0-aeef-ebfaeaa4dbb5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### The Filmmaker's Journey
Ruiz's path to documentary filmmaking is as fascinating as the films he creates. Born in Mexico to a father who spent his youth in a monastery and a white American mother from New York, Ruiz grew up navigating multiple cultures. His family relocated to New York when he was six, where he was immersed in Caribbean Latino culture--Puerto Rican and Dominican communities that shaped his understanding of the Latino diaspora's inherent diversity.
This unique perspective--being simultaneously inside and outside various Latino communities--has given Ruiz a deep appreciation for the inherent diversity and complexity of his community. It's this sensibility that makes his work so compelling and authentic.
### From Icons to Innovation
Ruiz's career has evolved from what he describes as "building monuments to our heroes"--like his biography of Roberto Clemente for American Experience--to taking greater creative risks. He compares his approach to running a small restaurant: "You say, I want to make food my way, and there are going to be people who love it."
His film Harvest Season exemplifies this evolution, exploring Latino winemakers and the largely invisible Latino labor that powers California's wine industry. When the devastating 2017 wildfires struck mid-production, Ruiz pivoted to document that crisis, demonstrating the adaptability and commitment required in documentary filmmaking.
### The Love-Hate Relationship
One of the most powerful observations Bernardo shared was about America's love-hate relationship with Latino communities. He pointed to the stark contrast between 2020, when Latino workers were celebrated as "essential" during the pandemic--nurses, delivery workers, agricultural laborers keeping the country running--and 2025, where we're witnessing raids targeting those same communities at their worksites.
This dynamic isn't new. It echoes through history--from the bracero program to cycles of deportation and recruitment. But capturing it on film, documenting these contradictions in real time, is what gives Bernardo's work its lasting power.
### Documenting the Latino Vote
Bernardo's work covering the Latino Vote in 2024 and 2020 exemplifies what happens when a filmmaker refuses to accept easy narratives. While most coverage of Latino voters relies on polls and punditry, Bernardo and his team spent months filming in eight states, talking to voters in their own communities, documenting the frustration and anger that conventional wisdom kept missing.
His documentaries don't just capture a moment - they capture a transformation. By focusing on real voices rather than predetermined narratives, Bernardo's documentary revealed the complexity that gets lost when we reduce millions of diverse Latino voters to a monolithic bloc. It's the kind of patient, observant filmmaking that discovers truth rather than imposing it.
### Looking Forward
Ruiz's current focus is on community building--creating what he calls a "chicharron circuit" for Latino artists, inspired by the chitlin circuit that sustained Black performers during segregation. In-person events, local gatherings, and grassroots audience building offer a way to transform narratives and strengthen community bonds during challenging times.
As we navigate this tumultuous moment in American history, voices like Bernardo Ruiz's remind us that our story is complex, our presence is undeniable, and our persistence is unshakeable. We're not going anywhere. We're America.

* * *
# **AOC spent nearly $50K on Puerto Rico hotels, meals while denouncing gentrification**
Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez's campaign dropped approximately **[$50,000 on luxury Puerto Rico accommodations](https://substack.com/redirect/89cfbc92-a47b-4dce-acbe-bfee82fecb7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** during the third quarter, including stays at exclusive colonial-era hotels while she publicly criticized gentrification on the island.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/89cfbc92-a47b-4dce-acbe-bfee82fecb7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **High-end lodging:** AOC's campaign spent $15,489.77 on Puerto Rico hotels between July and September, including over $11,000 at the "first-class, adults only" Hotel Palacio Provincial boasting "transcendent hints of the structure's grand colonial past" and nearly $4,000 at Hotel El Convento, plus at least $10,743 on meals and catering.
* **Concert venue expenses:** The campaign shelled out more than $23,000 renting the Coliseo De Puerto Rico on June 24 and August 25--the same venue where Ocasio-Cortez was filmed dancing at Bad Bunny's August concert alongside Brooklyn Representative Nydia Velazquez and celebrities including LeBron James and Penelope Cruz.
* **Mainland luxury spending:** Additional third-quarter expenditures included $6,600 at Hotel Vermont in Burlington during her "Fighting Oligarchy" tour with Senator Bernie Sanders, $2,000 at Manhattan's Thompson Central Park Hotel, $3,000 at Brooklyn's Arlo Williamsburg, and $6,300 for a single meal at a DC restaurant.

Campaign manager Oliver Hidalgo-Wohlleben defended the spending to Fox News, stating Ocasio-Cortez "regularly travels to Puerto Rico to support local causes and host events that require both staff and security."

# **Democrat lawmaker makes fool of himself: Calls DC National Guard murders "unfortunate accident"**
Mississippi Democratic Representative Bennie Thompson faced fierce backlash from the Trump administration and congressional Republicans after characterizing the deadly National Guard ambush near the White House as an **["unfortunate accident"](https://substack.com/redirect/2747a848-3586-4003-9243-90ea12ee0ca9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/2747a848-3586-4003-9243-90ea12ee0ca9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)during a Thursday hearing.
* **Swift reprimand:** Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem immediately interrupted Thompson's questioning: "It was a terrorist attack. He shot our Guardsmen in the head," while Representative Andy Ogles erupted that calling the murder "an unfortunate incident" was "f--king disrespectful," with White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt condemning the remarks as "disgraceful."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b5d3b079-acdc-432e-86e1-33033ba26601?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **Attack details:** Afghan national Rahmanullah Lakanwal executed National Guardswoman Sarah Beckstrom, 20, and critically wounded Guardsman Andrew Wolfe, 24, during a Thanksgiving Eve daylight assault just blocks from the White House as they patrolled the capital, with the suspect entering through Biden's Operation Allies Welcom
e program.
* **Broader terror concerns:** National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent testified the Intelligence Community identified approximately 2,000 known or suspected terrorists among 88,000 Afghan refugees admitted through the program, plus another 16,000 terror suspects who entered during Biden's term with ties to ISIS, al-Qaeda, Tren de Aragua, or MS-13.

* * *
# **Democrats join GOP to defeat Al Green 's latest Trump impeachment push**
Texas Representative Al Green's fifth impeachment attempt against President Trump collapsed Thursday after nearly two dozen **[Democrats sided with Republicans](https://substack.com/redirect/56754b14-3335-4d5d-90bc-aa20e6739531?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to dismiss the resolution, while party leadership abstained from supporting the measure.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/56754b14-3335-4d5d-90bc-aa20e6739531?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Cross-party defeat:** The tabling motion succeeded 237-140 with 47 abstentions, as 23 Democrats from competitive districts--including Tom Suozzi, Josh Riley, Jared Golden, and Chrissy Houlahan--voted alongside Republicans to block consideration, while top leaders Hakeem Jeffries, Katherine Clark, and Pete Aguilar chose "present" votes instea
[](https://substack.com/redirect/0f84879f-43be-460c-a811-3fbdbbad0d82?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
d.
* **Twin impeachment charges:** Green accused Trump of demanding "execution" for six lawmakers who released footage encouraging military personnel to disobey unlawful commands, which Trump called "seditious behavior...punishable by death," while creating an atmosphere where elected officials and jurists face threats.
* **Strategic party positioning:** Democratic leadership justified their abstentions by arguing proper impeachment demands extensive investigations, witness testimony, public hearings, and broad consensus-building--"None of that serious work has been done" given Republican control of the House focused on advancing Trump's priorities rather than accountability measures.

Green, removed from Trump's March congressional speech for disruptions, has repeatedly filed impeachment articles this year despite Jeffries acknowledging Republicans would never permit floor consideration since "Donald Trump will order them not to do it."

The Clayton Act of 1914, the second of the United States' major antitrust statutes, bans acquisitions and mergers when the effect "may be substantially to lessen competition, or to tend to create a monopoly." Under the guidelines of the Federal Trade Commission and the Justice Department, both mergers appear to "raise a presumption of illegality."But isn't this really about politics? And should that influence how you think?Some argue that the Netflix deal deserves support anyway because Paramount would be an even worse buyer. The idea is that David Ellison, the chief executive of Paramount, wants to build an evil media empire using his father's money and gut CNN, which Warner Bros. Discovery owns. Mr. Ellison's father, Larry, is one of the world's richest men and a major Republican donor close to President Trump.Basically, the idea is that one should cheer on the Netflix deal because otherwise the son of a friend of Trump will benefit.I can see the temptation to think that way, but you can't run a rule-based system like that. You can't look at every merger and try to decide whether it benefits or hurts friends of Trump -- that just makes the law revolve around him.The better view is to recognize that both deals would be bad for the country, and both should be challenged by antitrust authorities. Warner Bros. Discovery's streaming business is actually profitable as it is. It should just stay independent. And Warner Bros., if you must sell, maybe try finding a buyer who is not a direct competitor?The fact is that Netflix's proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery would be damaging not just in economic terms but also in terms of cultural creativity. In the long run, buying Warner Bros. would probably be as harmful for Netflix as it would be for Warner Bros. The combination of close rivals usually works out that way.Since its founding in 1923, Warner Bros. has made bold business and creative bets. In the late 1920s it was the first major studio to do sound films. It was one of the few to bet heavily on television in the 1950s. In the 1970s the larger Warner company pioneered superhero films, and starting in the late 1990s its HBO division essentially invented premium television with shows like "The Sopranos" and "The Wire." Many of its gambles have been contrarian, such as developing Looney Tunes as a goofier, more anarchic alternative to Disney's animation. That is what competition is supposed to do: force companies to carve out a niche for themselves.Netflix, for its part, is the greatest media innovator of the past decade. Transcending its modest origins as a DVD-by-mail service, it managed to succeed where earlier efforts to mix the internet and entertainment industries failed (such as Microsoft's). Netflix proved that streaming could be a viable business model. It also, for better or worse, pioneered the binge-release model (with "House of Cards") and so-called global originals (like "Squid Game").If Netflix and Warner Bros. Discovery were combined, it might be a cash cow, but the whole would be less than the sum of the parts. Netflix has suggested that it might keep HBO separate, but what parent company lets itself be outbid by its own unit? The more likely outcome is a bland mush -- the loss of a distinct sensibility within either operation.A Paramount acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery would not be better. In addition to having a significant overlap in streaming services, Paramount and Warner Bros. are direct competitors as major film studios with theatrical releases. Their merger, at least on those grounds, is also presumptively illegal.For those who want a more technical analysis: antitrust enforcers would point out that the two companies are direct competitors in premium streaming services, where Netflix is No. 1 and HBO-Discovery is No. 3 or 4, depending on which ranking system you use. Merging them would eliminate a head-to-head rival. That hurts consumers by making price increases easier, and it hurts sellers of films and TV by combining bidders. When the next equivalent of "The White Lotus" is being pitched, you expect Netflix and HBO to compete for it. Eliminating one of the two is pretty much the textbook antitrust definition of lost competition.So what will happen? I predict, either way, court challenges that last a year. It isn't clear right now who will win the battle to acquire Warner Bros. If it is Netflix, a federal challenge seems a near certainty, and I'd put the odds at greater than 50 percent that Netflix will lose -- but it will take time.If Paramount wins the takeover battle -- and if the federal government does bow out (perhaps, as some fear, because of an affinity between Mr. Trump and the Ellisons), something else may happen. California may well bring the challenge to protect workers in the film industry. California's attorney general, Rob Bonta, has been an active enforcer of the antitrust laws, so I think there are strong odds he sues to block a Paramount deal if the federal government folds.Why is Warner Bros. Discovery even selling? It is [spinning off its cable channels, ](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/5d1b850f?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)so the answer has little to do with its core business -- the streaming divisions are profitable -- and more to do with the burdensome costs of its previous inadvisable mergers. The disastrous acquisition in 2018 of Warner Bros. by AT&T (and the foolish failure of a judge to stop it) began the process. AT&T then spun off Warner Bros. and combined it with Discovery in 2022, saddling the merged company with billions of dollars in debt from merger financing. Ego-driven, hype-influenced decision-making -- the curse of the mogul -- has created this mess, not business fundamentals.Warner Bros. Discovery still makes money with entertainment that millions of Americans want to watch. After it finds a noncompeting buyer or collects the $5.8 billion fee that the offer requires Netflix to pay if regulators scuttle the deal, it should be in a good position to rise again.([A version of this ](https://the-antimonopolist.ghost.io/r/d57a07d3?m=46b412a0-1cbe-4fcb-b85d-2477ce9f4e21)post originally appeared in the New York Times).

Hi Peter!
Kelly Morrison here. In case you missed it: Indiana Senate Republicans just voted down a plan to redraw the state’s congressional districts to construct two more GOP leaning seats.
In a state where Republicans hold 40 of the 50 Senate seats, the redistricting plan was voted down 31-19. That means that 21 Republican Senators joined Democrats to stand against this unlawful gerrymandering despite the aggressive pressure from President Trump and his allies.
I am incredibly proud of the brave Indiana legislators, who have shown that they will not be bullied into acting against their convictions. Our President has the largest bully pulpit in the world and he uses it to get his way. This is another clear signal the American people are sending directly to Trump: enough is enough.
Peter, these 21 Republicans put their country over their party, and their courage will inspire leaders nationwide to take a stand against Trump. I firmly believe that courage is contagious . If we all did one thing each day that was a little bit brave, like these Indiana legislators, our country would move forward, not continue to be dragged back. I am inspired by all of you who continue to show courage and resilience in these tumultuous times, and fight back against this administration in a way that is authentic to you.
You all inspire me to be brave each and every day! Onwards to 2026.
With gratitude,
Kelly Morrison

body:
Here’s what Donald Trump said about me:
#
Peter, at this point, there’s nothing President Trump could say that would shock me. His tirades and rants make the news every day.
_And this week, he directed one at me._
Trump attacked me personally because he doesn’t like that I stand up to the far-right’s chaos and corruption. Even more than that, Trump is _terrified_ that this campaign can defeat his handpicked candidate here in NC and take back power for the American people.
Peter, I’m not afraid of the president calling me names or riling up his MAGA base against me. But I know that this is just the start of the GOP directing all their attention at us. We’ve seen it time and time again: When Donald Trump attacks a candidate, the GOP money-machine revs up against them, too.
**[I need your help to face what’s ahead. I’m asking you to split a donation between our campaign and State Democrats Committee in whatever you can afford so we can have the resources to fight back.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/98548?refcode=em20251211-9825&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=9825%2E614464%2EQyhl81)**
So, you may be wondering what exactly Trump said about me.
He called me a _“radical left lunatic.”_
**If fighting for lower prices, affordable health care, abortion access, voting rights, good schools, and a livable planet makes me a “radical left lunatic,” then so be it.**
You know where I stand and what I’m fighting for, Peter. I need to know if you’re with me.
**[I’m not asking because I want to, but because I have to. This is the most consequential Senate race on the map. Split a donation between our campaign and State Democrats Committee if you can, and help me take on Trump and the national GOP.](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/98548?refcode=em20251211-9825&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=9825%2E614464%2EQyhl81)**

---
Patriot,
---
Kathy Hochul is still _saying_ that she’ll comfortably win the governor’s race.
---
But actions speak louder than words – _and behind the scenes, Hochul is _acting_ like a candidate running in one of 2026’s **TOP battleground races**_!
---
Her latest move is bringing on veteran Democrat operatives who have worked on other recent top battleground races – including Michigan, Georgia, and Wisconsin – in a desperate bid to boost her struggling reelection campaign.
---
Yes, you read that right... The Democrats are so threatened by our grassroots campaign, that they’re now treating New York state like _Michigan, Georgia, and Wisconsin_!
---
**_New York Post_ : “Hochul beefs up campaign staff with battleground political veterans in sign of looming GOP threat”**
“Gov. Kathy Hochul is filling the upper echelons of her re-election team with alumni of campaigns in battleground states and other recent high-stakes political fights – a signal she may be **_expecting a tough race_** even in deep-blue New York.”
---
This PROVES what I’ve been saying all along: No state has moved further to the right in recent years than New York!
---
Forget all the conventional wisdom about New York being a “blue” state...
---
**With Hochul at the top of the ticket, New York is a TOP 2026 battleground – and like the polling shows, the governor’s race is currently a _TOSS-UP_. **
---
But winning a toss-up race like this means leaving no stone unturned.
---
